title.zh: 卷五十二 志第四: 曆一
title.raw: 卷五十二 志第四: 曆一 Volume 52 Treatises 5: Calendar 1

sentences.zh: 夫明時治曆，自黃帝、堯、舜與三代之盛王，莫不重之，其文備見於傳記矣。

translations.literal: As for clarifying the seasons and regulating the calendar, from the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun down to the flourishing kings of the Three Dynasties, none failed to attach weight to it; the full record of this appears in the historical narratives.
translations.idiomatic: Clarifying the seasons and regulating the calendar was esteemed by rulers from the Yellow Emperor through Yao and Shun to the greatest kings of the Three Dynasties; the full account survives in the historical records.

sentences.zh: 雖去古既遠，其法不詳，然原其要，不過隨時考驗，以合於天而已。

translations.literal: Although the age is already far from antiquity and the methods are not detailed, tracing their essentials, it is nothing more than testing in season so as to accord with Heaven—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Though we are far removed from antiquity and the methods are no longer fully known, the essential principle was always the same: observe and test as times require, until the calendar matches the heavens.

sentences.zh: 漢劉歆作《三統曆》，始立積年日法，以為推步之準。

translations.literal: Liu Xin of Han composed the Triple Concordance Calendar, first establishing accumulated years and day-divisors as the standard for astronomical computation.
translations.idiomatic: In the Han, Liu Xin wrote the Triple Concordance Calendar and was the first to set out accumulated years and day-tables as the basis for calendrical calculation.

sentences.zh: 後世因之，歷唐而宋，其更元改法者，凡數十家，豈故相為乖異哉？

translations.literal: Later ages followed this; from Tang through Song, those who changed the origin and revised the methods numbered several tens of houses—could they have intentionally made themselves mutually divergent?
translations.idiomatic: Later dynasties followed suit; from Tang through Song, dozens of schools revised the epoch and changed the methods—not because they wished to contradict one another.

sentences.zh: 蓋天有不齊之運，而曆為一定之法，所以既久而不能不差，既差則不可不改也。

translations.literal: For Heaven has inconstant cycles, while the calendar is a fixed method; therefore after long use discrepancy cannot be avoided, and once there is discrepancy it cannot go unrevised.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's motions are not perfectly uniform, yet a calendar must be a fixed system; over time errors inevitably accumulate, and once they appear the calendar must be revised.

sentences.zh: 元初承用金《大明曆》，庚辰歲，太祖西征，五月望，月蝕不效；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuan they continued to use the Jin Great Enlightenment Calendar; in the gengchen year, when the Grand Progenitor campaigned west, on the full moon of the fifth month the lunar eclipse did not match prediction;
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuan the court still used the Jin dynasty's Great Enlightenment Calendar; in a gengchen year, during the Grand Progenitor's western campaign, the lunar eclipse predicted for the fifteenth of the fifth month failed to occur as forecast;

sentences.zh: 二月、五月朔，微月見於西南。

translations.literal: On the first days of the second and fifth months, a sliver of moon was seen in the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: On new-moon days in the second and fifth months, a thin crescent appeared in the southwest when it should not have.

sentences.zh: 中書令耶律楚材以《大明曆》後天，乃損節氣之分，減周天之秒，去交終之率，治月轉之余，課兩曜之後先，調五行之出沒，以正《大明曆》之失。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Yelü Chucai, holding that the Great Enlightenment Calendar lagged behind Heaven, then reduced the divisions of the solar terms, diminished the seconds of the celestial revolution, removed the rate of nodal completion, regulated the remainder of lunar motion, examined the precedence of the two luminaries, and adjusted the rising and setting of the Five Planets, thereby correcting the errors of the Great Enlightenment Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Yelü Chucai judged the Great Enlightenment Calendar to run behind the heavens; he trimmed the solar-term divisions, reduced seconds in the tropical year, revised nodal-cycle rates, refined lunar-motion remainders, recalculated the sun and moon's relative positions, and adjusted planetary risings and settings to correct the calendar's errors.

sentences.zh: 且以中元庚午歲，國兵南伐，而天下略定，推上元庚午歲天正十一月壬戌朔，子正冬至，日月合璧，五星聯珠，同會虛宿六度，以應太祖受命之符。

translations.literal: Moreover, taking the middle origin in the gengwu year, when the state's armies marched south and the realm was largely settled, he projected the upper origin in the gengwu year: first month of the celestial year, eleventh month, renxu new moon, midnight winter solstice, sun and moon conjoined, the Five Planets strung like pearls, all meeting together at six degrees of the lodge Xu—thereby matching the token of the Grand Progenitor's receipt of the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: He also took the middle origin in a gengwu year—when imperial forces marched south and the realm was nearly pacified—and derived an upper origin in gengwu: on the winter solstice at midnight, new moon on renxu day in the eleventh month, with sun and moon united and the five planets aligned at six degrees of Xu, in token of the Grand Progenitor's Mandate.

sentences.zh: 又以西域、中原地裏殊遠，創為裏差以增損之，雖東西萬里，不復差忒。

translations.literal: Furthermore, because the Western Regions and the Central Plain lie far apart in latitude, he devised a latitude correction to add or subtract, so that though east and west were ten thousand li apart, discrepancy would no longer arise.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Western Regions and the Central Plain differ greatly in latitude, he invented a latitude correction so that observations thousands of li apart would no longer disagree.

sentences.zh: 遂題其名曰《西征庚午元曆》，表上之，然不果頒用。

translations.literal: He then entitled it the Western Campaign Gengwu Origin Calendar, memorialized it to the throne, yet it was in the end not promulgated for use.
translations.idiomatic: He titled the work the Western Campaign Gengwu Origin Calendar and submitted it to the throne, but it was never actually put into use.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，西域劄馬魯丁撰進《萬年曆》，世祖稍頒行之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan, Jamal al-Din of the Western Regions composed and presented the Myriad Years Calendar; the Shizu Emperor gradually promulgated it for use.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 4, Jamal al-Din from the Western Regions presented the Myriad Years Calendar, and Kublai gradually put it into circulation.

sentences.zh: 十三年，平宋，遂詔前中書左丞許衡、太子贊善王恂、都水少監郭守敬改治新曆。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, after the pacification of Song, an edict ordered the former Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Xu Heng, the Crown Prince's Tutor Wang Xun, and the Vice Director of the Waterways Guo Shoujing to revise and compile a new calendar.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13, after the conquest of Song, the court ordered Xu Heng, Wang Xun, and Guo Shoujing to draft a new calendar.

sentences.zh: 衡等以為金雖改曆，止以宋《紀元曆》微加增益，實未嘗測驗於天，乃與南北日官陳鼎臣、鄧元麟、毛鵬翼、劉巨淵、王素、嶽鉉、高敬等參考累代曆法，復測候日月星辰消息運行之變，參別同異，酌取中數，以為曆本。

translations.literal: Heng and the others held that although Jin had revised the calendar, it only slightly increased the Song Jiyuan Calendar and had in truth never tested against Heaven; they therefore joined the northern and southern calendar officials Chen Dingchen, Deng Yuanlin, Mao Pengyi, Liu Juyuan, Wang Su, Yue Xuan, Gao Jing, and others in consulting successive generations of calendrical methods, again observing and measuring the waxing and waning and motion of the sun, moon, stars, and planets, comparing similarities and differences, and selecting median values as the calendar's foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Heng and his colleagues argued that the Jin revision had merely tweaked the Song Jiyuan Calendar without genuine astronomical testing; with calendar officials from north and south they reviewed earlier systems, re-observed the motions of sun, moon, and planets, compared results, and chose balanced values as the new calendar's basis.

sentences.zh: 十七年冬至，曆成，詔賜名曰《授時曆》。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice of the seventeenth year the calendar was completed; an edict bestowed the name Season-Granting Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar was finished at the winter solstice of year 17, and the court named it the Season-Granting Calendar.

sentences.zh: 十八年，頒行天下。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year it was promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 it was issued empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 二十年，詔太子諭德李謙為《曆議》，發明新曆順天求合之微，考證前代人為附會之失，誠可以貽之永久，自古及今，其推驗之精，蓋未有出於此者也。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year an edict ordered the Crown Prince's Instructor Li Qian to compose a Discourse on the Calendar, expounding the subtlety by which the new calendar seeks accord with Heaven, verifying the errors of forced accommodation in earlier generations, truly fit to be handed down forever; from antiquity to the present, in the precision of its deductions and tests, probably none has surpassed this.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 Li Qian, instructor to the crown prince, was ordered to write a Discourse on the Calendar explaining how the new system aligns with the heavens and exposing earlier calendars' forced adjustments—a work fit to endure; in precision of calculation and verification, none had surpassed it.

sentences.zh: 今衡、恂、守敬等所撰《曆經》及謙《曆議》故存，皆可考據，是用具著於篇。

translations.literal: Now the Calendar Classic composed by Heng, Xun, Shoujing, and others, and Qian's Discourse on the Calendar, still survive and may all be consulted; therefore they are set forth in full in this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The Calendar Classic by Xu Heng, Wang Xun, and Guo Shoujing, and Li Qian's Discourse, still survive and can be verified; they are therefore recorded here in detail.

sentences.zh: 惟《萬年曆》不復傳，而《庚午元曆》雖未嘗頒用，其為書猶在，因附著於後，使來者有考焉。

translations.literal: Only the Myriad Years Calendar is no longer transmitted; but although the Gengwu Origin Calendar was never promulgated for use, the book still exists, and is therefore appended at the end so that those to come may have material for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The Myriad Years Calendar no longer survives, but the Gengwu Origin Calendar, though never adopted, is still extant and is appended here for future reference.

sentences.zh: 作《曆志》。

translations.literal: This composes the Treatise on the Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Treatise on the Calendar is composed.

sentences.zh: 授時曆議上驗氣

translations.literal: Discourse on the Season-Granting Calendar, Part I: Verifying the Qi
translations.idiomatic: Discourse on the Season-Granting Calendar, Part I: Verifying the Solar Terms

sentences.zh: 天道運行，如環無端，治曆者必就陰消陽息之際，以為立法之始。

translations.literal: The Way of Heaven moves in cycles without end; those who regulate the calendar must take the juncture where yin wanes and yang rests as the beginning of legislation.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's course runs in an endless cycle; calendar-makers must fix the moment when yin declines and yang pauses as the starting point for their system.

sentences.zh: 陰陽消息之機，何從而見之？

translations.literal: The mechanism of yin-yang waxing and waning—by what means can it be seen?
translations.idiomatic: How is one to detect the turning of yin and yang?

sentences.zh: 惟候其日晷進退，則其機將無所遁。

translations.literal: Only by observing the advance and retreat of the sundial shadow will that mechanism have nowhere to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Only by watching the gnomon shadow lengthen and shorten can that turning be captured with certainty.

sentences.zh: 候之之法，不過植表測景，以究其氣至之始。

translations.literal: The method of observing is nothing more than erecting a gnomon and measuring the shadow, thereby investigating the beginning of the arrival of qi.
translations.idiomatic: The method is simply to set up a gnomon, measure the shadow, and determine when each solar term arrives.

sentences.zh: 智作能述，前代諸人為法略備，茍能精思密索，心與理會，則前人述作之外，未必無所增益。

translations.literal: The wise devise and the able transmit; the men of former generations had methods largely complete—yet if one can think finely and search closely, with mind meeting principle, then beyond what predecessors composed there may yet be gains.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier masters had largely perfected the methods; yet with careful thought and close observation, aligning mind with principle, further improvements beyond their work remain possible.

sentences.zh: 舊法擇地平衍，設水準繩墨，植表其中，以度其中晷。

translations.literal: The old method chose level ground, set a water level and plumb line, planted the gnomon in the center, and thereby measured the central noon shadow.
translations.idiomatic: The old practice was to choose level ground, establish a true vertical with level and plumb line, set the gnomon at the center, and measure the noon shadow.

sentences.zh: 然表短促，尺寸之下所為分秒太、半、少之數，未易分別。

translations.literal: Yet when the gnomon was short, the fractional parts below an inch—major, half, and minor portions of fen and miao—were not easy to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: A short gnomon made it hard to read fine gradations of fen and miao below the inch mark.

sentences.zh: 表長，則分寸稍長，所不便者，景虛而淡，難得實景。

translations.literal: When the gnomon was long, the fen and cun were somewhat longer; the inconvenience was that the shadow was faint and diffuse, making a true shadow hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: A longer gnomon eased reading the scale, but the shadow grew faint and diffuse, making a precise edge difficult to capture.

sentences.zh: 前人欲就虛景之中考求真實，或設望筒，或置小表，或以木為規，皆取表端日光下徹圭面。

translations.literal: Predecessors wishing to seek the true within the diffuse shadow sometimes set sighting tubes, sometimes placed small gnomons, or used wooden gauges—all taking the sunlight from the tip of the gnomon down to the measuring surface.
translations.idiomatic: To extract a true reading from a blurred shadow, earlier observers used sighting tubes, auxiliary gnomons, or wooden templates—all channeling sunlight from the gnomon tip to the measuring plane.

sentences.zh: 今以銅為表，高三十六尺，端挾以二龍，舉一橫梁，下至圭面，共四十尺，是為八尺之表五。

translations.literal: Now a bronze gnomon is used, thirty-six feet high; at the top two dragons clasp a crossbeam, and from there down to the measuring surface is forty feet in all—equivalent to five eight-foot gnomons.
translations.idiomatic: The new gnomon is cast in bronze, thirty-six feet tall, with two dragons at the top holding a crossbeam; from crossbeam to measuring surface is forty feet—five times the classical eight-foot standard.

sentences.zh: 圭表刻為尺寸，舊寸一，今申而為五，厘毫差易分。

translations.literal: The measuring table is graduated in cun and chi; formerly one inch on the scale, now expanded to five, so that li and hao differences are easy to divide.
translations.idiomatic: The measuring table is marked in cun and chi; where the old scale used one division per inch, the new scale uses five, making fine readings of li and hao far easier.

sentences.zh: 別創為景符，以取實景。

translations.literal: A shadow template was separately devised to capture the true shadow.
translations.idiomatic: They also invented a shadow template to capture a sharp, true shadow image.

sentences.zh: 其制以銅葉，博二寸，長加博之二，中穿一竅，若針芥然，以方跂為趺，一端設為機軸，令可開闔，榰其一端，使其勢斜倚，北高南下，往來遷就於虛景之中，竅達日光，僅如米許，隱然見橫梁於其中。

translations.literal: Its form used a copper plate two inches wide, the length twice the width plus two, with a hole pierced through the center like a mustard seed; a square base served as the stand; one end was fitted with a pivot so it could open and close; one end was propped so that it leaned obliquely, high in the north and low in the south; moving back and forth within the diffuse shadow, when sunlight passed through the hole only about the size of a grain of rice, the crossbeam was dimly visible within.
translations.idiomatic: It was a copper plate two inches wide and four inches long, pierced with a pinhole at the center, mounted on a square base with a hinged pivot so one end could be tilted north-high, south-low; slid within the blurred shadow until a pinhole beam the size of a rice grain fell through and the crossbeam appeared faintly inside.

sentences.zh: 舊法以表端測晷，所得者日體上邊之景，今以橫梁取之，實得中景，不容有毫末之差。

translations.literal: The old method measured the noon shadow from the tip of the gnomon and obtained the shadow of the sun's upper limb; now the crossbeam is used, truly obtaining the central shadow, allowing no fraction of difference.
translations.idiomatic: The old method measured from the gnomon tip and captured the upper limb of the sun; the crossbeam method yields the sun's center, eliminating even the slightest error.

sentences.zh: 地中八尺表景，冬至長一丈三尺有奇，夏至尺有五寸。

translations.literal: At the earth's center, the shadow of the eight-foot gnomon at winter solstice is a little over one zhang and three chi long; at summer solstice, one chi and five cun.
translations.idiomatic: At the geographical center, an eight-foot gnomon casts a shadow of somewhat more than thirteen feet at winter solstice and one foot five inches at summer solstice.

sentences.zh: 今京師長表，冬至之景七丈九尺八寸有奇，在八尺表則一丈五尺九寸六分；

translations.literal: Now at the capital with the long gnomon, the winter-solstice shadow is a little over seven zhang, nine chi, and eight cun; reduced to the eight-foot gnomon it would be one zhang, five chi, nine cun, and six fen;
translations.idiomatic: At the capital the long gnomon gives a winter-solstice shadow of nearly seventy-nine chi eight cun; scaled to an eight-foot gnomon that is fifteen chi nine cun six fen;

sentences.zh: 夏至之景一丈一尺七寸有奇，在八尺表則二尺三寸四分。

translations.literal: the summer-solstice shadow is a little over one zhang, one chi, and seven cun; on the eight-foot gnomon, two chi, three cun, and four fen.
translations.idiomatic: the summer-solstice shadow is a little over eleven chi seven cun; on an eight-foot gnomon, two chi three cun four fen.

sentences.zh: 雖晷景長短所在不同，而其景長為冬至，景短為夏至，則一也。

translations.literal: Although the length of the noon shadow differs from place to place, that the long shadow is winter solstice and the short shadow summer solstice is the same everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Shadow lengths differ by latitude, but everywhere the longest shadow marks winter solstice and the shortest marks summer solstice.

sentences.zh: 惟是氣至時刻考求不易，蓋至日氣正，則一歲氣節從而正矣。

translations.literal: Only the determination of the moment when qi arrives is not easy to seek; for if the solstice day's qi is correct, then the year's solar terms follow and are correct.
translations.idiomatic: Pinpointing the exact moment of solstice is difficult; yet if the solstice is fixed correctly, the entire year's solar terms fall into place.

sentences.zh: 劉宋祖沖之嘗取至前後二十三四日間晷景，折取其中，定為冬至，且以日差比課，推定時刻。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi of Liu Song once took noon shadows from about twenty-three or twenty-four days before and after the solstice, halved the mean between them, and fixed winter solstice, moreover using daily difference ratios to calculate and fix the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi of Liu Song measured noon shadows for roughly twenty-three or twenty-four days on either side of solstice, took the midpoint as winter solstice, and used daily shadow differences to compute the exact moment.

sentences.zh: 宋皇祐間，周琮則取立冬、立春二日之景，以為去至既遠，日差頗多，易為推考。

translations.literal: In Song during Huangyou, Zhou Cong took the shadows of the Beginning of Winter and Beginning of Spring days, holding that being far from the solstice, the daily difference was rather large and easy to use in calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song Emperor Renzong, Zhou Cong used shadows on Beginning of Winter and Beginning of Spring, arguing that being far from solstice the daily change was larger and easier to calculate with.

sentences.zh: 《紀元》以後諸曆，為法加詳，大抵不出沖之之法。

translations.literal: Calendars after the Jiyuan largely added detail to the methods but for the most part did not depart from Chongzhi's method.
translations.idiomatic: Post-Jiyuan calendars refined the procedures but largely followed Zu Chongzhi's approach.

sentences.zh: 新曆積日累月，實測中晷，自遠日以及近日，取前後日率相埒者，參考同異，初非偏取一二日之景，以取數多者為定，實減《大明曆》一十九刻二十分。

translations.literal: The new calendar accumulated days and months of actual measurement of noon shadows, from distant days to near days, taking days before and after whose rates matched, comparing similarities and differences—not at first selectively taking the shadow of one or two days and fixing by whichever numbers were more numerous; it in fact reduced the Great Enlightenment Calendar by nineteen ke and twenty fen.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar relied on months of actual noon-shadow measurements, comparing days with similar daily rates before and after solstice rather than cherry-picking one or two readings; it shortened the Great Enlightenment Calendar's solstice by nineteen ke twenty fen.

sentences.zh: 仍以累歲實測中晷日差分寸，定擬二至時刻於後。

translations.literal: Still using the fen and cun of daily noon-shadow difference from accumulated years of actual measurement, the moments of the two solstices are fixed below.
translations.idiomatic: Using years of measured daily shadow differences, the solstice moments are determined as follows.

sentences.zh: 推至元十四年丁丑歲冬至

translations.literal: Computation of the winter solstice in the dingchou year, the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan
translations.idiomatic: Calculating the winter solstice of Zhiyuan 14 (dingchou year)

sentences.zh: 其年十一月十四日己亥，景長七丈九尺四寸八分五厘五毫；

translations.literal: In that year, on the fourteenth day of the eleventh month, jihai day, the shadow length was seven zhang, nine chi, four cun, eight fen, five li, and five hao;
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth of the eleventh month (jihai day) that year, the shadow measured seven zhang nine chi four cun eight fen five li five hao;

sentences.zh: 至二十一日丙午，景長七丈九尺五寸四分一厘；

translations.literal: to the twenty-first day, bingwu day, shadow length seven zhang, nine chi, five cun, four fen, one li;
translations.idiomatic: by the twenty-first (bingwu day) it was seven zhang nine chi five cun four fen one li;

sentences.zh: 二十二日丁未，景長七丈九尺四寸五分五厘。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day, dingwei day, shadow length seven zhang, nine chi, four cun, five fen, five li.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second (dingwei day) it was seven zhang nine chi four cun five fen five li.

sentences.zh: 以己亥、丁未二日之景相校，余三分五毫為晷差，進二位；

translations.literal: Comparing the shadows of the jihai and dingwei days, the remainder of three fen and five hao is taken as the gnomon difference, advanced two places;
translations.idiomatic: Comparing the jihai and dingwei shadows leaves a gnomon difference of three fen five hao, carried forward two decimal places;

sentences.zh: 以丙午、丁未二日之景相校，余八分六厘為法；

translations.literal: comparing the shadows of bingwu and dingwei days, the remainder of eight fen and six li is taken as the divisor;
translations.idiomatic: comparing bingwu and dingwei shadows gives a divisor of eight fen six li;

sentences.zh: 除之，得三十五刻；

translations.literal: dividing, one obtains thirty-five ke;

sentences.zh: 用減相距日八百刻，余七百六十五刻；

translations.literal: subtracting from the eight hundred ke between the days, seven hundred sixty-five ke remain;
translations.idiomatic: subtracting from eight hundred ke between the days leaves seven hundred sixty-five ke;

sentences.zh: 折取其中，加半日刻，共為四百三十二刻半；

translations.literal: halving this and adding half a day's ke, the total is four hundred thirty-two and a half ke;
translations.idiomatic: halving and adding half a day gives four hundred thirty-two and a half ke;

sentences.zh: 百約為日，得四日；

translations.literal: reducing by hundreds to days, four days are obtained;
translations.idiomatic: converting by hundreds gives four days;

sentences.zh: 余以十二乘之，百約為時，得三時，滿五十又作一時，共得四時；

translations.literal: the remainder multiplied by twelve, reduced by hundreds to double-hours, yields three double-hours; when fifty fills, another double-hour is made, four double-hours in all;
translations.idiomatic: multiplying the remainder by twelve and converting gives three double-hours; rounding up at fifty adds another, for four double-hours total;

sentences.zh: 余以十二收之，得三刻；

translations.literal: the remainder collected by twelve gives three ke;
translations.idiomatic: the remainder divided by twelve gives three ke;

sentences.zh: 命初起距日己亥算外，得癸卯日辰初三刻為丁丑歲冬至。

translations.literal: counting from the initial jihai day of separation, outside the count one obtains guimao day, the third ke of the chen double-hour, as the winter solstice of the dingchou year.
translations.idiomatic: counting forward from jihai day yields guimao day at the third ke of chen hour as the dingchou winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後四日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from four days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This calculation uses shadows from four days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 十一月初九日甲午，景七丈八尺六寸三分五厘五毫；

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the eleventh month, jiawu day, shadow seven zhang, eight chi, six cun, three fen, five li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth of the eleventh month (jiawu day), shadow seven zhang eight chi six cun three fen five li five hao;

sentences.zh: 至二十六日辛亥，景七丈八尺七寸九分三厘五毫；

translations.literal: to the twenty-sixth day, xinhai day, shadow seven zhang, eight chi, seven cun, nine fen, three li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: by the twenty-sixth (xinhai day), shadow seven zhang eight chi seven cun nine fen three li five hao;

sentences.zh: 二十七日壬子，景七丈八尺五寸五分。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day, renzi day, shadow seven zhang, eight chi, five cun, five fen.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh (renzi day), shadow seven zhang eight chi five cun five fen.

sentences.zh: 以甲午、壬子景相減，復以辛亥、壬子景相減，準前法求之，亦得癸卯日辰初三刻。

translations.literal: Subtracting the jiawu and renzi shadows, then subtracting the xinhai and renzi shadows, and seeking by the previous method, one again obtains guimao day, third ke of chen hour.
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting jiawu from renzi and xinhai from renzi shadows and applying the same method again yields guimao day, third ke of chen hour.

sentences.zh: 至二十八日癸丑，景七丈八尺三寸四厘五毫，用壬子、癸丑二日之景與甲午景，準前法求之，亦合。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day, guichou day, shadow seven zhang, eight chi, three cun, four li, five hao; using the shadows of renzi and guichou days with the jiawu shadow and seeking by the previous method, it also agrees.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth (guichou day) the shadow was seven zhang eight chi three cun four li five hao; using renzi, guichou, and jiawu shadows with the same method also agrees.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後八九日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from eight or nine days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from eight or nine days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙戌朔，景七丈五尺九寸八分六厘五毫；

translations.literal: On the new moon of the eleventh month, bingxu day, shadow seven zhang, five chi, nine cun, eight fen, six li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: On new moon of the eleventh month (bingxu day), shadow seven zhang five chi nine cun eight fen six li five hao;

sentences.zh: 二日丁亥，景七丈六尺三寸七分七厘；

translations.literal: on the second day, dinghai day, shadow seven zhang, six chi, three cun, seven fen, seven li;
translations.idiomatic: on the second (dinghai day), shadow seven zhang six chi three cun seven fen seven li;

sentences.zh: 至十二月初六日庚申，景七丈五尺八寸五分一厘。

translations.literal: to the sixth day of the twelfth month, gengshen day, shadow seven zhang, five chi, eight cun, five fen, one li.
translations.idiomatic: by the sixth of the twelfth month (gengshen day), shadow seven zhang five chi eight cun five fen one li.

sentences.zh: 準前法求之，亦在辰初三刻。

translations.literal: Seeking by the previous method, it also falls at the third ke of chen hour.
translations.idiomatic: Applying the same method again gives the third ke of chen hour.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後一十七日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from seventeen days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from seventeen days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 十月二十一日丙子，景七丈九寸七分一厘；

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the tenth month, bingzi day, shadow seven zhang, nine cun, seven fen, one li;
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first of the tenth month (bingzi day), shadow seven zhang nine cun seven fen one li;

sentences.zh: 至十二月十六日庚午，景七丈七寸六分；

translations.literal: to the sixteenth day of the twelfth month, gengwu day, shadow seven zhang, seven cun, six fen;
translations.idiomatic: by the sixteenth of the twelfth month (gengwu day), shadow seven zhang seven cun six fen;

sentences.zh: 十七日辛未，景七丈一寸五分六厘五毫。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day, xinwei day, shadow seven zhang, one chi, five fen, six li, five hao.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth (xinwei day), shadow seven zhang one chi five fen six li five hao.

sentences.zh: 準前法求之，亦得辰初三刻。

translations.literal: Seeking by the previous method, one again obtains the third ke of chen hour.
translations.idiomatic: The same method again yields the third ke of chen hour.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後二十七日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from twenty-seven days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from twenty-seven days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 六月初五日癸亥，景一丈三尺八分；

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the sixth month, guihai day, shadow one zhang, three chi, eight fen;
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth of the sixth month (guihai day), shadow one zhang three chi eight fen;

sentences.zh: 距十五年五月癸未朔，景一丈三尺三分八厘五毫；

translations.literal: at the separation of the fifteenth year, fifth month, guimao new moon, shadow one zhang, three chi, three fen, eight li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: at the fifteenth year's fifth-month new moon (guimao day), shadow one zhang three chi three fen eight li five hao;

sentences.zh: 初二日甲申，景一丈二尺九寸二分五毫。

translations.literal: On the second day, jiashen day, shadow one zhang, two chi, nine cun, two fen, five hao.
translations.idiomatic: On the second (jiashen day), shadow one zhang two chi nine cun two fen five hao.

sentences.zh: 準前法求之，亦合。

translations.literal: Seeking by the previous method, it also agrees.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後一百六十日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from one hundred sixty days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from one hundred sixty days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 推十五年戊寅歲夏至

translations.literal: Computation of the summer solstice in the wuyin year, the fifteenth year
translations.idiomatic: Calculating the summer solstice of year 15 (wuyin year)

sentences.zh: 五月十九日辛丑，景一丈一尺七寸七分七厘五毫；

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day of the fifth month, xinchou day, shadow one zhang, one chi, seven cun, seven fen, seven li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth of the fifth month (xinchou day), shadow one zhang one chi seven cun seven fen seven li five hao;

sentences.zh: 距二十八日庚戌，景一丈一尺七寸八分；

translations.literal: at the separation of the twenty-eighth day, gengxu day, shadow one zhang, one chi, seven cun, eight fen;
translations.idiomatic: by the twenty-eighth (gengxu day), shadow one zhang one chi seven cun eight fen;

sentences.zh: 二十九日辛亥，景一丈一尺八寸五厘五毫。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day, xinhai day, shadow one zhang, one chi, eight cun, five li, five hao.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth (xinhai day), shadow one zhang one chi eight cun five li five hao.

sentences.zh: 用辛丑、庚戌二日之景相減，余二厘五毫，進二位為實；

translations.literal: Subtracting the shadows of xinchou and gengxu days, the remainder of two li and five hao, advanced two places, is the dividend;
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting xinchou and gengxu shadows leaves two li five hao as dividend, carried two places;

sentences.zh: 復用庚戌、辛亥景相減，余二分五厘五毫為法；

translations.literal: again subtracting the gengxu and xinhai shadows, the remainder of two fen, five li, five hao is the divisor;
translations.idiomatic: subtracting gengxu and xinhai shadows gives a divisor of two fen five li five hao;

sentences.zh: 除之，得九刻，用減相距日九百刻，余八百九十一刻；

translations.literal: dividing, nine ke are obtained; subtracting from the nine hundred ke between days, eight hundred ninety-one ke remain;
translations.idiomatic: division yields nine ke; subtracting from nine hundred ke between days leaves eight hundred ninety-one ke;

sentences.zh: 半之，加半日刻，百約，得四日；

translations.literal: halving, adding half a day's ke, reducing by hundreds, four days are obtained;
translations.idiomatic: halving, adding half a day, and converting by hundreds gives four days;

sentences.zh: 余以十二乘之，百約，得十一時；

translations.literal: the remainder multiplied by twelve, reduced by hundreds, yields eleven double-hours;
translations.idiomatic: multiplying the remainder by twelve and converting gives eleven double-hours;

sentences.zh: 余以十二收為刻，得三刻；

translations.literal: the remainder collected by twelve as ke gives three ke;
translations.idiomatic: the remainder divided by twelve gives three ke;

sentences.zh: 命初起距日辛丑算外，得乙巳日亥正三刻夏至。

translations.literal: counting from the initial xinchou day of separation, outside the count one obtains yisi day, the third ke of the midnight hour of hai, as summer solstice.
translations.idiomatic: counting forward from xinchou day yields yisi day at the third ke of midnight (hai hour) as summer solstice.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後四日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from four days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This calculation uses shadows from four days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 十四年十二月十五日己巳，景七丈一尺三寸四分三厘；

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the twelfth month of the fourteenth year, jisi day, shadow seven zhang, one chi, three cun, four fen, three li;
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth of the twelfth month of year 14 (jisi day), shadow seven zhang one chi three cun four fen three li;

sentences.zh: 距十五年十一月初二日辛巳，景七丈七寸五分九厘五毫；

translations.literal: at the separation of the second day of the eleventh month of the fifteenth year, xinsi day, shadow seven zhang, seven cun, five fen, nine li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: at the second of the eleventh month of year 15 (xinsi day), shadow seven zhang seven cun five fen nine li five hao;

sentences.zh: 初三日壬午，景七丈一尺四寸六厘。

translations.literal: On the third day, renwu day, shadow seven zhang, one chi, four cun, six li.
translations.idiomatic: On the third (renwu day), shadow seven zhang one chi four cun six li.

sentences.zh: 用己巳、壬午景相減，以辛巳、壬午景相減除之，亦合。

translations.literal: Subtracting the jisi and renwu shadows, and dividing by the subtraction of xinsi and renwu shadows, it also agrees.
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting jisi and renwu shadows and dividing by xinsi-minus-renwu also agrees.

sentences.zh: 此用至前後一百五十六日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from one hundred fifty-six days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from one hundred fifty-six days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 十四年十二月十二日丙寅，景七丈二尺九寸七分二厘五毫；

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the twelfth month of the fourteenth year, bingyin day, shadow seven zhang, two chi, nine cun, seven fen, two li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth of the twelfth month of year 14 (bingyin day), shadow seven zhang two chi nine cun seven fen two li five hao;

sentences.zh: 十三日丁卯，景七丈二尺四寸五分四厘五毫；

translations.literal: on the thirteenth day, dingmao day, shadow seven zhang, two chi, four cun, five fen, four li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: on the thirteenth (dingmao day), shadow seven zhang two chi four cun five fen four li five hao;

sentences.zh: 十四日戊辰，景七丈一尺九寸九厘；

translations.literal: on the fourteenth day, wuchen day, shadow seven zhang, one chi, nine cun, nine li;
translations.idiomatic: on the fourteenth (wuchen day), shadow seven zhang one chi nine cun nine li;

sentences.zh: 距十五年十一月初四日癸未，景七丈一尺九寸五分七厘五毫；

translations.literal: at the separation of the fourth day of the eleventh month of the fifteenth year, guimao day, shadow seven zhang, one chi, nine cun, five fen, seven li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: at the fourth of the eleventh month of year 15 (guimao day), shadow seven zhang one chi nine cun five fen seven li five hao;

sentences.zh: 初五日甲申，景七丈二尺五寸五厘；

translations.literal: on the fifth day, jiashen day, shadow seven zhang, two chi, five cun, five li;
translations.idiomatic: on the fifth (jiashen day), shadow seven zhang two chi five cun five li;

sentences.zh: 初六日乙酉，景七丈三尺三分三厘五毫。

translations.literal: on the sixth day, yiyou day, shadow seven zhang, three chi, three fen, three li, five hao.
translations.idiomatic: on the sixth (yiyou day), shadow seven zhang three chi three fen three li five hao.

sentences.zh: 前後互取，所得時刻皆合。

translations.literal: Taking from before and after reciprocally, the resulting times all agree.
translations.idiomatic: Using shadows from either side reciprocally, all resulting times agree.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後一百五十八九日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from one hundred fifty-eight or nine days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from one hundred fifty-eight or nine days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 十四年十二月初七日辛酉，景七丈五尺四寸一分七厘；

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the twelfth month of the fourteenth year, xinyou day, shadow seven zhang, five chi, four cun, one fen, seven li;
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh of the twelfth month of year 14 (xinyou day), shadow seven zhang five chi four cun one fen seven li;

sentences.zh: 初八日壬戌，景七丈四尺九寸五分九厘五毫；

translations.literal: on the eighth day, renxu day, shadow seven zhang, four chi, nine cun, five fen, nine li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: on the eighth (renxu day), shadow seven zhang four chi nine cun five fen nine li five hao;

sentences.zh: 初九日癸亥，景七丈四尺四寸八分六厘；

translations.literal: on the ninth day, guihai day, shadow seven zhang, four chi, four cun, eight fen, six li;
translations.idiomatic: on the ninth (guihai day), shadow seven zhang four chi four cun eight fen six li;

sentences.zh: 距十五年十一月初九日戊子，景七丈四尺五寸二分五毫；

translations.literal: at the separation of the ninth day of the eleventh month of the fifteenth year, wuzi day, shadow seven zhang, four chi, five cun, two fen, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: at the ninth of the eleventh month of year 15 (wuzi day), shadow seven zhang four chi five cun two fen five hao;

sentences.zh: 初十日己丑，景七丈五尺三厘五毫；

translations.literal: on the tenth day, jichou day, shadow seven zhang, five chi, three li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: on the tenth (jichou day), shadow seven zhang five chi three li five hao;

sentences.zh: 十一日庚寅，景七丈五尺四寸四分九厘五毫。

translations.literal: on the eleventh day, gengyin day, shadow seven zhang, five chi, four cun, four fen, nine li, five hao.
translations.idiomatic: on the eleventh (gengyin day), shadow seven zhang five chi four cun four fen nine li five hao.

sentences.zh: 以壬戌、己丑景相減為實，以辛酉、壬戌景相減為法，除之；

translations.literal: Subtracting the renxu and jichou shadows is taken as the dividend; subtracting the xinyou and renxu shadows is taken as the divisor; dividing;
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting renxu from jichou shadows gives the dividend, xinyou-minus-renxu the divisor; dividing;

sentences.zh: 或以壬戌、癸亥景相減，或以戊子、己丑景相減，若己丑、庚寅景相減，推前法求之，皆合。

translations.literal: Or subtracting the renxu and guihai shadows, or subtracting the wuzi and jichou shadows, or subtracting the jichou and gengyin shadows, and seeking by the previous method—all agree.
translations.idiomatic: Whether subtracting renxu and guihai, wuzi and jichou, or jichou and gengyin shadows and applying the previous method, all agree.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後一百六十三四日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from one hundred sixty-three or four days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from one hundred sixty-three or four days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 推十五年戊寅歲冬至

translations.literal: Computation of the winter solstice in the wuyin year, the fifteenth year
translations.idiomatic: Calculating the winter solstice of year 15 (wuyin year)

sentences.zh: 其年十一月十九日戊戌，景七丈八尺三寸一分八厘五毫；

translations.literal: In that year, on the nineteenth day of the eleventh month, wuxu day, shadow seven zhang, eight chi, three cun, one fen, eight li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth of the eleventh month that year (wuxu day), shadow seven zhang eight chi three cun one fen eight li five hao;

sentences.zh: 距閏十一月初九日戊午，景七丈八尺三寸六分三厘五毫；

translations.literal: at the separation of the ninth day of the intercalary eleventh month, wuwu day, shadow seven zhang, eight chi, three cun, six fen, three li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: at the ninth of the intercalary eleventh month (wuwu day), shadow seven zhang eight chi three cun six fen three li five hao;

sentences.zh: 初十日己未，景七丈八尺八分二厘五毫。

translations.literal: on the tenth day, jiwei day, shadow seven zhang, eight chi, eight fen, two li, five hao.
translations.idiomatic: on the tenth (jiwei day), shadow seven zhang eight chi eight fen two li five hao.

sentences.zh: 用戊戌、戊午二日景相減，余四分五厘為晷差，進二位，以戊午、己未景相減，余二寸八分一厘為法，除之，得一十六刻，加相距日二千刻，半之，加半日刻，百約，得十日；

translations.literal: Subtracting the shadows of wuxu and wuwu days, the remainder of four fen and five li is taken as the gnomon difference, advanced two places; subtracting the wuwu and jiwei shadows, the remainder of two cun, eight fen, one li is taken as the divisor; dividing, sixteen ke are obtained; adding the two thousand ke between the days, halving, adding half a day's ke, reducing by hundreds, ten days are obtained;
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting wuxu and wuwu shadows leaves a gnomon difference of four fen five li, carried two places; subtracting wuwu and jiwei shadows gives a divisor of two cun eight fen one li; dividing yields sixteen ke; adding two thousand ke between days, halving, adding half a day, and converting by hundreds gives ten days;

sentences.zh: 余以十二乘之，百約為時，滿五十又進一時，共得七時；

translations.literal: the remainder multiplied by twelve, reduced by hundreds to double-hours, when fifty fills another double-hour is added, seven double-hours in all;
translations.idiomatic: multiplying the remainder by twelve and converting gives seven double-hours, rounding up at fifty;

sentences.zh: 余以十二收為刻；

translations.literal: the remainder collected by twelve gives ke;
translations.idiomatic: the remainder divided by twelve gives ke;

sentences.zh: 命初起距日己亥算外，得戊申日未初三刻為戊寅歲冬至。

translations.literal: counting from the initial jihai day of separation, outside the count one obtains wushen day, the third ke of the wei double-hour, as the winter solstice of the wuyin year.
translations.idiomatic: counting forward from jihai day yields wushen day at the third ke of wei hour as the wuyin winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後十日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from ten days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This calculation uses shadows from ten days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 十一月十二日辛卯，景七丈五尺八寸八分一厘五毫；

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the eleventh month, xinmao day, shadow seven zhang, five chi, eight cun, eight fen, one li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth of the eleventh month (xinmao day), shadow seven zhang five chi eight cun eight fen one li five hao;

sentences.zh: 十三日壬辰，景七丈六尺三寸一厘五毫；

translations.literal: on the thirteenth day, renchen day, shadow seven zhang, six chi, three cun, one li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: on the thirteenth (renchen day), shadow seven zhang six chi three cun one li five hao;

sentences.zh: 閏十一月十五日甲子，景七丈六尺三寸六分六厘五毫；

translations.literal: on the fifteenth day of the intercalary eleventh month, jiazi day, shadow seven zhang, six chi, three cun, six fen, six li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: on the fifteenth of the intercalary eleventh month (jiazi day), shadow seven zhang six chi three cun six fen six li five hao;

sentences.zh: 十六日乙丑，景七丈五尺九寸五分三厘；

translations.literal: on the sixteenth day, yichou day, shadow seven zhang, five chi, nine cun, five fen, three li;
translations.idiomatic: on the sixteenth (yichou day), shadow seven zhang five chi nine cun five fen three li;

sentences.zh: 十七日丙寅，景七丈五尺五寸四厘五毫。

translations.literal: on the seventeenth day, bingyin day, shadow seven zhang, five chi, five cun, four li, five hao.
translations.idiomatic: on the seventeenth (bingyin day), shadow seven zhang five chi five cun four li five hao.

sentences.zh: 用壬辰、甲子景相減為實，以辛卯、壬辰景相減為法，除之，亦得戊申日未初三刻。

translations.literal: Subtracting the renchen and jiazi shadows is taken as the dividend; subtracting the xinmao and renchen shadows is taken as the divisor; dividing, one again obtains wushen day, the third ke of wei hour.
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting renchen and jiazi shadows as dividend and xinmao-minus-renchen as divisor yields wushen day at the third ke of wei hour.

sentences.zh: 或用甲子、乙丑景相減，推之，亦合。

translations.literal: Or subtracting the jiazi and yichou shadows and computing—it also agrees.
translations.idiomatic: Using jiazi-minus-yichou shadows and applying the method also agrees.

sentences.zh: 若用辛卯、乙丑景相減為實，用乙丑、丙寅景相減，除之，並同。

translations.literal: If one subtracts the xinmao and yichou shadows as the dividend and subtracts the yichou and bingyin shadows as the divisor, dividing—the result is the same.
translations.idiomatic: Using xinmao-minus-yichou as dividend and yichou-minus-bingyin as divisor gives the same result.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後十六七日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from sixteen or seventeen days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from sixteen or seventeen days on either side of solstice.

translations.literal: Subtracting the jiawu and guiyou shadows, subtracting the guisi and jiawu shadows, and computing by the previous method—the result is also the same.
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting jiawu and guiyou shadows and guisi-minus-jiawu and applying the same method gives the same result.

sentences.zh: 若以壬申、癸酉景相減為法，推之亦同。

translations.literal: If one takes the subtraction of the renshen and guiyou shadows as the divisor and computes, the result is also the same.
translations.idiomatic: Using renshen-minus-guiyou shadows as the divisor and applying the same method also agrees.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後十八九日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from eighteen or nineteen days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from eighteen or nineteen days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 若用癸巳與甲戌景相減，以壬辰、癸巳景相減，推之，或癸巳、甲午景相減，推之，或用甲戌、癸酉景相減，推之，或甲戌、乙亥景相減，推之，或以壬辰、乙亥景相減，用壬辰、癸巳景相減，推之並同。

translations.literal: If one subtracts the guisi and jiaxu shadows, subtracts the renchen and guisi shadows, and computes; or subtracts the guisi and jiawu shadows and computes; or subtracts the jiaxu and guiyou shadows and computes; or subtracts the jiaxu and yihai shadows and computes; or subtracts the renchen and yihai shadows, using the subtraction of the renchen and guisi shadows, and computes—all agree.
translations.idiomatic: Whether one subtracts guisi-minus-jiaxu, renchen-minus-guisi, guisi-minus-jiawu, jiaxu-minus-guiyou, jiaxu-minus-yihai, or renchen-minus-yihai paired with renchen-minus-guisi and applies the same method, all agree.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後二十日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from twenty days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from twenty days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 十月十六日庚寅，景七丈三尺一分五厘；

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day of the tenth month, gengyin day, shadow seven zhang, three chi, one fen, five li;
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth of the tenth month (gengyin day), shadow seven zhang three chi one fen five li;

sentences.zh: 十二月初三日丙子，景七丈三尺三寸二分；

translations.literal: on the third day of the twelfth month, bingzi day, shadow seven zhang, three chi, three cun, two fen;
translations.idiomatic: on the third of the twelfth month (bingzi day), shadow seven zhang three chi three cun two fen;

sentences.zh: 初四日丁丑，景七丈二尺八寸四分二厘五毫。

translations.literal: on the fourth day, dingchou day, shadow seven zhang, two chi, eight cun, four fen, two li, five hao.
translations.idiomatic: on the fourth (dingchou day), shadow seven zhang two chi eight cun four fen two li five hao.

sentences.zh: 用庚寅、丁丑景相減，以丙子、丁丑景相減，推之亦同。

translations.literal: Subtracting the gengyin and dingchou shadows, subtracting the bingzi and dingchou shadows, and computing—the result is also the same.
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting gengyin and dingchou shadows and bingzi-minus-dingchou and applying the same method gives the same result.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後二十三日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from twenty-three days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from twenty-three days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 十月十四日戊子，景七丈一尺九寸二分二厘五毫；

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the tenth month, wuzi day, shadow seven zhang, one chi, nine cun, two fen, two li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth of the tenth month (wuzi day), shadow seven zhang one chi nine cun two fen two li five hao;

sentences.zh: 十五日己丑，景七丈二尺四寸六分九厘；

translations.literal: on the fifteenth day, jichou day, shadow seven zhang, two chi, four cun, six fen, nine li;
translations.idiomatic: on the fifteenth (jichou day), shadow seven zhang two chi four cun six fen nine li;

sentences.zh: 十二月初五日戊寅，景七丈二尺二寸七分二厘五毫。

translations.literal: on the fifth day of the twelfth month, wuyin day, shadow seven zhang, two chi, two cun, seven fen, two li, five hao.
translations.idiomatic: on the fifth of the twelfth month (wuyin day), shadow seven zhang two chi two cun seven fen two li five hao.

sentences.zh: 用己丑、戊寅景相減，以戊子、己丑景相減，推之，或用己丑、庚寅相減，推之亦同。

translations.literal: Subtracting the jichou and wuyin shadows, subtracting the wuzi and jichou shadows, and computing; or subtracting jichou and gengyin and computing—the result is also the same.
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting jichou and wuyin shadows and wuzi-minus-jichou, or jichou-minus-gengyin, and applying the same method gives the same result.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後二十四日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from twenty-four days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from twenty-four days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 十月初七日辛巳，景六丈七尺七寸四分五厘；

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the tenth month, xinsi day, shadow six zhang, seven chi, seven cun, four fen, five li;
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh of the tenth month (xinsi day), shadow six zhang seven chi seven cun four fen five li;

sentences.zh: 初八日壬午，景六丈八尺三寸七分二厘五毫；

translations.literal: on the eighth day, renwu day, shadow six zhang, eight chi, three cun, seven fen, two li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: on the eighth (renwu day), shadow six zhang eight chi three cun seven fen two li five hao;

sentences.zh: 初九日癸未，景六丈八尺九寸七分七厘五毫；

translations.literal: on the ninth day, guiwei day, shadow six zhang, eight chi, nine cun, seven fen, seven li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: on the ninth (guiwei day), shadow six zhang eight chi nine cun seven fen seven li five hao;

sentences.zh: 十二月十二日乙酉，景六丈八尺一寸四分五厘。

translations.literal: on the twelfth day of the twelfth month, yiyou day, shadow six zhang, eight chi, one cun, four fen, five li.
translations.idiomatic: on the twelfth of the twelfth month (yiyou day), shadow six zhang eight chi one cun four fen five li.

sentences.zh: 用壬午、乙酉景相減，以辛巳、壬午相減，推之，壬午、癸未景相減，推之亦同。

translations.literal: Subtracting the renwu and yiyou shadows, subtracting xinsi and renwu, and computing; subtracting the renwu and guiwei shadows and computing—the result is also the same.
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting renwu and yiyou shadows and xinsi-minus-renwu, or renwu-minus-guiwei, and applying the same method gives the same result.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後三十一二日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from thirty-one or two days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from thirty-one or two days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 十月乙亥朔，景六丈三尺八寸七分；

translations.literal: On the new moon of the tenth month, yihai day, shadow six zhang, three chi, eight cun, seven fen;
translations.idiomatic: On new moon of the tenth month (yihai day), shadow six zhang three chi eight cun seven fen;

sentences.zh: 十二月十八日辛卯，景六丈四尺二寸九分七厘五毫；

translations.literal: on the eighteenth day of the twelfth month, xinmao day, shadow six zhang, four chi, two cun, nine fen, seven li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: on the eighteenth of the twelfth month (xinmao day), shadow six zhang four chi two cun nine fen seven li five hao;

sentences.zh: 十九日壬辰，景六丈三尺六寸二分五厘。

translations.literal: on the nineteenth day, renchen day, shadow six zhang, three chi, six cun, two fen, five li.
translations.idiomatic: on the nineteenth (renchen day), shadow six zhang three chi six cun two fen five li.

sentences.zh: 用乙亥、壬辰景相減，以辛卯、壬辰景相減，推之亦同。

translations.literal: Subtracting the yihai and renchen shadows, subtracting the xinmao and renchen shadows, and computing—the result is also the same.
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting yihai and renchen shadows and xinmao-minus-renchen and applying the same method gives the same result.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後三十八日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from thirty-eight days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from thirty-eight days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 九月二十二日丙寅，景五丈七尺八寸二分五厘；

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day of the ninth month, bingyin day, shadow five zhang, seven chi, eight cun, two fen, five li;
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second of the ninth month (bingyin day), shadow five zhang seven chi eight cun two fen five li;

sentences.zh: 十二月二十八日辛丑，景五丈七尺五寸八分；

translations.literal: on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month, xinchou day, shadow five zhang, seven chi, five cun, eight fen;
translations.idiomatic: on the twenty-eighth of the twelfth month (xinchou day), shadow five zhang seven chi five cun eight fen;

sentences.zh: 二十九日壬寅，景五丈六尺九寸一分五厘。

translations.literal: on the twenty-ninth day, renyin day, shadow five zhang, six chi, nine cun, one fen, five li.
translations.idiomatic: on the twenty-ninth (renyin day), shadow five zhang six chi nine cun one fen five li.

sentences.zh: 用丙寅、辛丑景相減，以辛丑、壬寅景相減，推之亦同。

translations.literal: Subtracting the bingyin and xinchou shadows, subtracting the xinchou and renyin shadows, and computing—the result is also the same.
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting bingyin and xinchou shadows and xinchou-minus-renyin and applying the same method gives the same result.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後四十七八日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from forty-seven or eight days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from forty-seven or eight days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 九月二十日甲子，景五丈六尺四寸九分二厘五毫；

translations.literal: On the twentieth day of the ninth month, jiazi day, shadow five zhang, six chi, four cun, nine fen, two li, five hao;
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth of the ninth month (jiazi day), shadow five zhang six chi four cun nine fen two li five hao;

sentences.zh: 至十二月二十九日壬寅，景五丈六尺九寸一分五厘；

translations.literal: to the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month, renyin day, shadow five zhang, six chi, nine cun, one fen, five li;
translations.idiomatic: by the twenty-ninth of the twelfth month (renyin day), shadow five zhang six chi nine cun one fen five li;

sentences.zh: 至十七年正月癸卯朔，景五丈六尺二寸五分。

translations.literal: to the new moon of the first month of the seventeenth year, guimao day, shadow five zhang, six chi, two cun, five fen.
translations.idiomatic: by new moon of the first month of year 17 (guimao day), shadow five zhang six chi two cun five fen.

sentences.zh: 用甲子、癸卯相減，壬寅、癸卯景相減，推之亦同。

translations.literal: Subtracting jiazi and guimao, subtracting the renyin and guimao shadows, and computing—the result is also the same.
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting jiazi-minus-guimao and renyin-minus-guimao shadows and applying the same method gives the same result.

sentences.zh: 此取至前後五十日景。

translations.literal: This uses shadows from fifty days before and after the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: This uses shadows from fifty days on either side of solstice.

sentences.zh: 右以累年推測到冬夏二至時刻為準，定擬至元十八年辛巳歲前冬至，當在己未日夜半後六刻，即丑初一刻。

translations.literal: Above, taking as standard the winter and summer solstice moments derived from accumulated years of calculation, it is fixed and proposed that the winter solstice before the xinsi year, the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan, should fall on jiwei day, six ke after midnight, that is, the first ke of the chou double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: On the basis of solstice moments computed from years of observation, the winter solstice before Zhiyuan 18 (xinsi year) is fixed at jiwei day, six ke after midnight—the first ke of chou hour.

sentences.zh: 歲餘歲差

translations.literal: Year Remainder and Precession

sentences.zh: 周天之度，周歲之日，皆三百六十有五。

translations.literal: The degrees of a full circuit of Heaven and the days of a full circuit of the year are both three hundred sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: A full circuit of the heavens and a full tropical year both number three hundred sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 全策之外，又有奇分，大率皆四分之一。

translations.literal: Beyond the full tally, there are odd fractions; for the most part all are one quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the whole number there is always a fractional remainder, generally one quarter.

sentences.zh: 自今歲冬至距來歲冬至，曆三百六十五日，而日行一周，凡四周，曆千四百六十，則餘一日，析而四之，則四分之一也。

translations.literal: From this year's winter solstice to next year's winter solstice, one counts three hundred sixty-five days; the sun's daily motion completes one circuit; in four circuits one counts one thousand four hundred sixty, and one day remains; dividing it by four, one quarter is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: From one winter solstice to the next is three hundred sixty-five days; the sun completes one circuit per year, and in four years—one thousand four hundred sixty days—one day remains; divided by four, that is one quarter.

sentences.zh: 然天之分常有餘，歲之分常不足，其數有不能齊者，惟其所差至微，前人初未覺知。

translations.literal: Yet Heaven's fraction is often in surplus and the year's fraction often in deficit; their numbers cannot always be made equal—only the discrepancy is extremely slight, and predecessors at first did not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's fraction tends to run slightly high and the year's fraction slightly low; the two cannot always be made to match—but the difference is minuscule, and earlier astronomers did not notice it at first.

sentences.zh: 迨漢末劉洪，始覺冬至後天，謂歲周余分太強，乃作《乾象曆》，減歲餘分二千五百為二千四百六十二。

translations.literal: Not until Liu Hong at the end of Han did one first perceive that winter solstice lagged behind Heaven, holding that the surplus fraction of the year's circuit was too strong; he then composed the Supernal Image Calendar, reducing the year-remainder fraction from two thousand five hundred to two thousand four hundred sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Liu Hong in late Han did anyone notice that winter solstice ran behind the heavens; judging the year's surplus fraction too large, he wrote the Supernal Image Calendar and cut the year-remainder fraction from 2500 to 2462.

sentences.zh: 至晉虞喜，宋何承天、祖沖之，謂歲當有差，因立歲差之法。

translations.literal: Down to Yu Xi of Jin and He Chengtian and Zu Chongzhi of Song, who held that the year ought to have a discrepancy, the method of precession of the equinoxes was thereby established.
translations.idiomatic: By Jin's Yu Xi and Song's He Chengtian and Zu Chongzhi, who argued that the year must drift against the stars, the method of precession was established.

sentences.zh: 其法損歲餘，益天周，使歲餘浸弱，天周浸強，強弱相減，因得日躔歲退之差。

translations.literal: Its method reduced the year remainder and increased the celestial circuit, making the year remainder gradually weaker and the celestial circuit gradually stronger; subtracting strong from weak, one thereby obtained the discrepancy of the sun's lodge motion retreating against the year.
translations.idiomatic: The method trimmed the year remainder and enlarged the celestial circuit, gradually weakening the former and strengthening the latter; subtracting the two yields the rate at which the sun's position retreats year by year.

sentences.zh: 歲餘、天周，二者實相為用，歲差由斯而立，日躔由斯而得，一或損益失當，詎能與天葉哉？

translations.literal: The year remainder and the celestial circuit—the two in truth mutually serve; precession is established thereby, and the sun's lodge motion obtained thereby; if either increase or decrease is misplaced, how could one accord with Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Year remainder and celestial circuit work in tandem: precession and solar lodge position both depend on them. If either is adjusted wrongly, how can the calendar match the heavens?

sentences.zh: 今自劉宋大明壬寅以來，凡測景驗氣得冬至時刻真數者有六，取相距積日時刻，以相距之年除之，各得其時所用歲餘。

translations.literal: Now from the renyin year of the Great Enlightenment era of Liu Song down to the present, there are six instances of measuring shadows and testing qi to obtain the true number of the winter-solstice moment; taking the accumulated days and ke between each pair and dividing by the years between them, one obtains the year remainder used at each time.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liu Song's Great Enlightenment renyin year, six winter-solstice moments have been fixed by shadow measurement and qi testing; dividing the elapsed days and ke between each pair by the intervening years yields the year remainder used in each era.

sentences.zh: 復自大明壬寅距至元戊寅積日時刻，以相距之年除之，得每歲三百六十五日二十四分二十五秒，比《大明曆》減去一十一秒，定為方今所用歲餘。

translations.literal: Again, from Great Enlightenment renyin to Zhiyuan wuyin, taking the accumulated days and ke and dividing by the years between, one obtains three hundred sixty-five days, twenty-four fen, and twenty-five miao per year—eleven miao less than the Great Enlightenment Calendar—fixed as the year remainder now in use.
translations.idiomatic: From Great Enlightenment renyin to Zhiyuan wuyin, dividing total elapsed days and ke by the years between gives 365 days 24 fen 25 miao per year—11 miao less than the Great Enlightenment Calendar—fixed as the present year remainder.

sentences.zh: 余七十五秒，用益所謂四分之一，共為三百六十五度二十五分七十五秒，定為天周。

translations.literal: Adding seventy-five miao to the so-called one quarter, the total is three hundred sixty-five degrees, twenty-five fen, and seventy-five miao, fixed as the celestial circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Adding 75 miao to the nominal quarter-day gives 365 degrees 25 fen 75 miao, fixed as the celestial circuit.

sentences.zh: 余分強弱相減，余一分五十秒，用除全度，得六十六年有奇，日卻一度，以六十六年除全度，適得一分五十秒，定為歲差。

translations.literal: Subtracting the strong from the weak among the remainder fractions, one fen and fifty miao remain; dividing the full degrees by this, one obtains a little over sixty-six years for the sun to retreat one degree; dividing the full degrees by sixty-six years, one exactly obtains one fen and fifty miao, fixed as precession.
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting the surplus and deficit fractions leaves 1 fen 50 miao; dividing the full circle by this gives just over sixty-six years per degree of solar retreat; dividing the full circle by sixty-six years yields exactly 1 fen 50 miao, fixed as the precession rate.

sentences.zh: 復以《堯典》中星考之，其時冬至日在女、虛之交。

translations.literal: Examining again by the culminating stars of the Canon of Yao, at that time the winter-solstice sun was at the junction of Nu and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Checking against the culminating stars recorded in the Canon of Yao, the winter-solstice sun then stood at the border of the Nu and Xu lodges.

sentences.zh: 及考之前史，漢元和二年，冬至日在鬥二十一度；

translations.literal: Examining earlier histories, in the second year of Yuanhe of Han, the winter-solstice sun was at twenty-one degrees of Dipper;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories record that in Han Yuanhe 2 the winter-solstice sun stood at 21 degrees of the Dipper lodge;

sentences.zh: 晉太元九年，退在鬥十七度；

translations.literal: in the ninth year of Taiyuan of Jin, it had retreated to seventeen degrees of Dipper;
translations.idiomatic: by Jin Taiyuan 9 it had retreated to 17 degrees of Dipper;

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉十年，在鬥十四度末；

translations.literal: in the tenth year of Yuanjia of Song, it was at the end of fourteen degrees of Dipper;
translations.idiomatic: by Song Yuanjia 10 it stood near the end of 14 degrees of Dipper;

sentences.zh: 梁大同十年，在鬥十二度；

translations.literal: in the tenth year of Datong of Liang, it was at twelve degrees of Dipper;
translations.idiomatic: by Liang Datong 10 it stood at 12 degrees of Dipper;

sentences.zh: 隋開皇十八年，猶在鬥十二度；

translations.literal: in the eighteenth year of Kaihuang of Sui, it was still at twelve degrees of Dipper;
translations.idiomatic: by Sui Kaihuang 18 it still stood at 12 degrees of Dipper;

sentences.zh: 唐開元十二年，在鬥九度半；

translations.literal: in the twelfth year of Kaiyuan of Tang, it was at nine and a half degrees of Dipper;
translations.idiomatic: by Tang Kaiyuan 12 it stood at 9½ degrees of Dipper;

sentences.zh: 今退在箕十度。

translations.literal: Now it has retreated to ten degrees of Winnowing Basket.
translations.idiomatic: Today it has retreated to 10 degrees of the Winnowing Basket lodge.

sentences.zh: 取其距今之年、距今之度較之，多者七十餘年，少者不下五十年，輒差一度。

translations.literal: Comparing the years from each to the present with the degrees from each to the present, where the years are more than seventy, or not less than fifty, the difference is one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing elapsed years with degrees of retreat, intervals of fifty to seventy-plus years consistently show one degree of difference.

sentences.zh: 宋慶元間，改《統天曆》，取大衍歲差率八十二年及開元所距之差五十五年，折取其中，得六十七年，為日卻行一度之差。

translations.literal: During the Qingyuan era of Song, when the Total Heaven Calendar was revised, taking the Dayan precession rate of eighty-two years and the fifty-five-year interval from Kaiyuan, halving the mean between them, sixty-seven years were obtained as the rate at which the sun retreats one degree.
translations.idiomatic: When Song revised the Total Heaven Calendar in the Qingyuan era, it split the difference between the Dayan rate of 82 years and the 55-year interval since Kaiyuan, yielding 67 years per degree of solar retreat.

sentences.zh: 施之今日，質諸天道，實為密近。

translations.literal: Applied to the present day and tested against Heaven's Way, it is truly close and precise.
translations.idiomatic: Applied to the present and tested against observation, it proves remarkably close.

sentences.zh: 然古今曆法，合於今必不能通於古，密於古必不能驗於今。

translations.literal: Yet in calendrical methods ancient and modern, what fits the present necessarily cannot extend to antiquity, and what is precise for antiquity necessarily cannot be verified in the present.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no calendar can fit both past and present: one accurate for today will fail antiquity, and one precise for antiquity will miss today.

sentences.zh: 今《授時曆》，以之考古，則增歲餘而損歲差；

translations.literal: Now the Season-Granting Calendar, used to investigate antiquity, increases the year remainder and reduces precession;
translations.idiomatic: The Season-Granting Calendar, applied to antiquity, increases the year remainder and reduces the precession rate;

sentences.zh: 以之推來，則增歲差而損歲餘；

translations.literal: used to project forward, it increases precession and reduces the year remainder;
translations.idiomatic: projected forward, it increases precession and reduces the year remainder;

sentences.zh: 上推春秋以來冬至，往往皆合；

translations.literal: projecting upward, winter solstices since the Spring and Autumn era mostly all agree;
translations.idiomatic: projecting backward, winter solstices since the Spring and Autumn era mostly agree;

sentences.zh: 下求方來，可以永久而無弊；

translations.literal: seeking downward into the future, it can endure permanently without flaw;
translations.idiomatic: projected forward, it can serve indefinitely without error;

sentences.zh: 非止密於今日而已。
