sentences.zh: 右自春秋獻公以來，凡二千一百六十餘年，用《大衍》、《宣明》、《紀元》、《統天》、《大明》、《授時》六曆推算冬至，凡四十九事。

translations.literal: Above, from Duke Xian of the Spring and Autumn period onward, more than 2,160 years in all, using the six calendars Great Concordance, Manifest Brightness, Era Origin, Total Heaven, Great Enlightenment, and Season-Granting to calculate winter solstice—forty-nine cases in total.
translations.idiomatic: From Duke Xian through 2,160+ years, six calendars were tested against forty-nine recorded winter solstices.

sentences.zh: 《大衍曆》合者三十二，不合者十七；

translations.literal: Great Concordance Calendar: thirty-two agree, seventeen disagree;

sentences.zh: 《宣明曆》合者二十六，不合者二十三；

translations.literal: Manifest Brightness Calendar: twenty-six agree, twenty-three disagree;

sentences.zh: 《紀元曆》合者三十五，不合者十四；

translations.literal: Era Origin Calendar: thirty-five agree, fourteen disagree;

sentences.zh: 《統天曆》合者三十八，不合者十一；

translations.literal: Total Heaven Calendar: thirty-eight agree, eleven disagree;

sentences.zh: 《大明曆》合者三十四，不合者十五；

translations.literal: Great Enlightenment Calendar: thirty-four agree, fifteen disagree;

sentences.zh: 《授時曆》合者三十九，不合者十事。

translations.literal: Season-Granting Calendar: thirty-nine agree, ten disagree.

sentences.zh: 今按獻公十五年戊寅歲正月甲寅朔旦冬至，《授時曆》得甲寅，《統天曆》得乙卯，後天一日；

translations.literal: Now examining Duke Xian year 15 (wuyin), new moon of the first month on jiayin day at dawn, winter solstice: Season-Granting gives jiayin; Total Heaven gives yimao—one day late;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xian year 15: Shoushi gives jiayin; Tongtian gives yimao, one day late;

sentences.zh: 至僖公五年丙寅歲正月辛亥朔旦冬至，《授時》、《統天》皆得辛亥，與天合；

translations.literal: down to Duke Xi year 5 (bingyin), new moon of the first month on xinhai day at dawn, winter solstice: Season-Granting and Total Heaven both give xinhai, matching Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xi year 5: both Shoushi and Tongtian give xinhai, matching the heavens;

sentences.zh: 下至昭公二十年己卯歲正月己丑朔旦冬至，《授時》、《統天》皆得戊子，並先一日，若曲變其法以從之，則獻公、僖公皆不合矣。

translations.literal: and down to Duke Zhao year 20 (jimao), new moon of the first month on jichou day at dawn, winter solstice: Season-Granting and Total Heaven both give wuzi, each one day early; if one twisted the methods to follow this, Duke Xian and Duke Xi would both fail to match.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao year 20: both calendars give wuzi, one day early; forcing a fit would break the earlier matches.

sentences.zh: 以此知《春秋》所書昭公冬至，乃日度失行之驗。

translations.literal: From this one knows that the winter solstice recorded for Duke Zhao in the Spring and Autumn Annals is evidence of the sun's motion having strayed.
translations.idiomatic: This shows the Spring and Autumn record for Duke Zhao reflects solar motion error, not calendar fault.

sentences.zh: 一也。

translations.literal: First.

sentences.zh: 《大衍曆》考古冬至，謂劉宋元嘉十三年丙子歲十一月甲戌日南至，《大衍》與《皇極》、《麟德》三曆皆得癸酉，各先一日，乃日度失行，非三曆之差。

translations.literal: The Great Concordance Calendar's investigation of ancient winter solstices holds that in Liu Song Yuanjia 13 (bingzi), sun at southern limit on jiaxu day in the eleventh month: Dayan, Huangji, and Linde all give guiyou, each one day early—it was the sun's motion that strayed, not error in the three calendars.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 13: Dayan, Huangji, and Linde all give guiyou, one day early—solar motion error, not calendar error.

sentences.zh: 今以《授時曆》考之，亦得癸酉。

translations.literal: Examined now with the Season-Granting Calendar, it too gives guiyou.

sentences.zh: 二也。

translations.literal: Second.

sentences.zh: 大明五年辛丑歲十一月乙酉冬至，諸曆皆得甲申，殆亦日度之差。

translations.literal: Daming 5 (xinchou), eleventh month, winter solstice on yiyou day: all calendars give jiashen—likely also solar motion error.
translations.idiomatic: Daming 5: all calendars give jiashen; likely solar motion error again.

sentences.zh: 三也。

translations.literal: Third.

sentences.zh: 陳太建四年壬辰歲十一月丁卯景長，《大衍》、《授時》皆得丙寅，是先一日；

translations.literal: Chen Taijian 4 (renchen), eleventh month, dingmao day longest shadow: Dayan and Shoushi both give bingyin—one day early;
translations.idiomatic: Taijian 4: Dayan and Shoushi both give bingyin, one day early;

sentences.zh: 太建九年丁酉歲十一月壬辰景長，《大衍》、《授時》皆得癸巳，是後一日；

translations.literal: Taijian 9 (dingyou), eleventh month, renchen day longest shadow: Dayan and Shoushi both give guisi—one day late;
translations.idiomatic: Taijian 9: Dayan and Shoushi both give guisi, one day late;

sentences.zh: 一失之先，一失之後，若合於壬辰，則差於丁酉，合於丁酉，則差於壬辰，亦日度失行之驗。

translations.literal: one erring early, one late; matching renchen would miss dingyou, and matching dingyou would miss renchen—again evidence of solar motion error.
translations.idiomatic: One early, one late; matching one year breaks the other—solar motion error.

sentences.zh: 五也。

translations.literal: Fifth.

sentences.zh: 開皇十一年辛亥歲十一月丙午景長，《大衍》、《統天》、《授時》皆得丙午，與天合；

translations.literal: Kaihuang 11 (xinhai), eleventh month, bingwu day longest shadow: Dayan, Tongtian, and Shoushi all give bingwu, matching Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 11: all three calendars give bingwu, matching the heavens;

sentences.zh: 至開皇十四年甲寅歲十一月辛酉冬至，而《大衍》、《統天》、《授時》皆得壬戌，若合於辛亥，則失於甲寅，合於甲寅，則失於辛亥，其開皇十四年甲寅歲冬至，亦日度失行。

translations.literal: but at Kaihuang 14 (jiayin), eleventh month, xinyou day winter solstice, Dayan, Tongtian, and Shoushi all give renxu; matching xinhai would miss jiayin, and matching jiayin would miss xinhai—the Kaihuang 14 winter solstice also reflects solar motion error.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 14: all give renxu; the recorded solstice again reflects solar motion error.

sentences.zh: 六也。

translations.literal: Sixth.

sentences.zh: 唐貞觀十八年甲辰歲十一月乙酉景長，諸曆得甲申，貞觀二十三年己酉歲十一月辛亥景長，諸曆皆得庚戌，《大衍曆議》以永淳、開元冬至推之，知前二冬至乃史官依時曆以書，必非候景所得，所以不合，今以《授時曆》考之亦然。

translations.literal: Tang Zhenguan 18 (jiachen), eleventh month, yiyou day longest shadow: calendars give jiashen; Zhenguan 23 (jiyou), eleventh month, xinhai day longest shadow: all give gengxu. The Dayan Calendar Discourse, extrapolating from Yongchun and Kaiyuan winter solstices, knew the prior two were written by historiographers from contemporary calendars, not from shadow observation—hence the mismatch; examined with Shoushi Calendar, the same holds.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 18 and 23 shadow records were historiographers' calendar entries, not gnomon observations—Shoushi confirms Dayan's judgment.

sentences.zh: 八也。

translations.literal: Eighth.

sentences.zh: 自前宋以來，測景驗氣者凡十七事，其景德丁未歲戊辰日南至，《統天》、《授時》皆得丁卯，是先一日；

translations.literal: Since Former Song, shadow and qi verification records number seventeen cases. Jingde dingwei year, wuchen day sun at southern limit: Tongtian and Shoushi both give dingmao—one day early;
translations.idiomatic: Song verification: Jingde winter solstice—Tongtian and Shoushi give dingmao, one day early;

sentences.zh: 嘉泰癸亥歲甲戌日南至，《統天》、《授時》皆得乙亥，是後一日；

translations.literal: Jiatai guihai year, jiaxu day sun at southern limit: Tongtian and Shoushi both give yihai—one day late;
translations.idiomatic: Jiatai winter solstice—both give yihai, one day late;

sentences.zh: 一失之先，一失之後，若曲變其數以從景德，則其餘十六事多後天，從嘉泰，則其餘十六事多先天，亦日度失行之驗。

translations.literal: one early, one late; twisting numbers to fit Jingde would make the other sixteen mostly late; fitting Jiatai would make them mostly early—again solar motion error.
translations.idiomatic: Fitting one case breaks the other fifteen—solar motion error.

sentences.zh: 十也。

translations.literal: Tenth.

sentences.zh: 前十事皆《授時曆》所不合，以此理推之，非不合矣，蓋類其同則知其中，辨其異則知其變。

translations.literal: The prior ten cases are all where Shoushi Calendar disagrees; reasoning from this principle, they are not true disagreements—group what matches to find the center, distinguish what differs to know the change.
translations.idiomatic: The ten mismatches reflect solar error; grouping agreements reveals the pattern.

sentences.zh: 今於冬至略其日度失行及史官依時曆書之者凡十事，則《授時曆》三十九事皆中，《統天曆》與今曆不合者僅有獻公一事，《大衍曆》推獻公冬至後天二日，《大明》後天三日，《授時曆》與天合。

translations.literal: Setting aside the ten cases of solar motion error and historiographers writing from contemporary calendars, Shoushi Calendar matches all thirty-nine remaining cases; Tongtian disagrees only on Duke Xian; Dayan is two days late on Duke Xian, Daming three days late; Shoushi matches Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Excluding ten error cases, Shoushi matches all 39; Tongtian misses only Duke Xian; Dayan and Daming run late.

sentences.zh: 下推至元庚辰冬至，《大衍》後天八十一刻，《大明》後天一十九刻，《統天曆》先天一刻，《授時曆》與天合。

translations.literal: Projecting forward to Zhiyuan gengchen winter solstice: Dayan is eighty-one ke late, Daming nineteen ke late, Tongtian one ke early; Shoushi matches Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Forward to Zhiyuan gengchen: Shoushi alone matches; Dayan 81 ke late, Daming 19 ke late.

sentences.zh: 以前代諸曆校之，《授時》為密，庶幾千歲之日至，可坐而致云。

translations.literal: Compared with earlier calendars, Shoushi is most precise; perhaps the solstice a millennium hence may be obtained without rising from one's seat.
translations.idiomatic: Among all calendars, Shoushi is most precise—the solstice of ages hence may be calculated at desk.

sentences.zh: 古今曆參校疏密

translations.literal: Comparing Ancient and Modern Calendars for Precision

sentences.zh: 《授時曆》與古曆相校，疏密自見，蓋上能合於數百載之前，則下可行之永久，此前人定說。

translations.literal: Comparing Shoushi Calendar with ancient calendars, precision and error show themselves; if it matches centuries past, it can run far into the future—this is the settled doctrine of earlier masters.
translations.idiomatic: If a calendar fits centuries back, it will hold for ages forward—an established principle.

sentences.zh: 古稱善治曆者，若宋何承天，隋劉焯，唐傅仁均、僧一行之流，最為傑出。

translations.literal: Ancient masters of calendrical science—Song's He Chengtian, Sui's Liu Chuo, Tang's Fu Renjun and the monk Yixing—were most outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian, Liu Chuo, Fu Renjun, and Yixing were the greatest calendar-makers.

sentences.zh: 今以其曆與至元庚辰冬至氣應相校，未有不舛戾者，而以新曆上推往古，無不吻合，則其疏密從可知已。

translations.literal: Comparing their calendars with the Zhiyuan gengchen winter solstice, none fail to diverge; yet projecting Shoushi Calendar backward, all match—its precision is thus known.
translations.idiomatic: Their calendars miss the Zhiyuan solstice; Shoushi matches every ancient case—its superiority is clear.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉十九年壬午歲十一月乙巳日十一刻冬至，距本朝至元十七年庚辰歲，計八百三十八年。

translations.literal: Song Emperor Wen Yuanjia 19 (renwu), eleventh month, yisi day, eleventh ke winter solstice—838 years from Zhiyuan 17 (gengchen).

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，氣應己未六刻冬至，《元嘉曆》推之，得辛酉，後《授時》二日，《授時》上考元嘉壬午歲冬至，得乙巳，與元嘉合。

translations.literal: That eleventh month, qi arrival at jiwei, sixth ke winter solstice: Yuankai Calendar gives xinyou, two days after Shoushi; Shoushi back-calculated to Yuanjia renwu gives yisi, matching Yuankai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai misses by two days; Shoushi back-calculation matches Yuankai exactly.

sentences.zh: 隋大業三年丁卯歲十一月庚午日五十二刻冬至，距至元十七年庚辰歲，計六百七十三年。

translations.literal: Sui Daye 3 (dingmao), eleventh month, gengwu day, fifty-two ke winter solstice—673 years from Zhiyuan 17.

sentences.zh: 《皇極曆》推之，得庚申冬至，後《授時》一日；

translations.literal: Huangji Calendar gives gengshen winter solstice, one day after Shoushi;
translations.idiomatic: Huangji gives gengshen, one day after Shoushi;

sentences.zh: 《授時》上考大業丁卯歲冬至，得庚午，與《皇極》合。

translations.literal: Shoushi back-calculated to Daye dingmao gives gengwu, matching Huangji.

sentences.zh: 唐武德元年戊寅歲十一月戊辰日六十四刻冬至，距至元十七年庚辰歲，計六百六十二年。

translations.literal: Tang Wude 1 (wuyin), eleventh month, wuchen day, sixty-four ke winter solstice—662 years from Zhiyuan 17.

sentences.zh: 《戊寅曆》推之，得庚申冬至，後《授時》一日；

translations.literal: Wuyin Calendar gives gengshen winter solstice, one day after Shoushi;
translations.idiomatic: Wuyin Calendar gives gengshen, one day after Shoushi;

sentences.zh: 《授時曆》上考武德戊寅歲，得戊辰冬至，與《戊寅曆》合。

translations.literal: Shoushi back-calculated to Wude wuyin gives wuchen winter solstice, matching Wuyin Calendar.

sentences.zh: 開元十五年丁卯歲十一月己亥日七十二刻冬至，距至元十七年庚辰歲，計五百五十三年。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan 15 (dingmao), eleventh month, jihai day, seventy-two ke winter solstice—553 years from Zhiyuan 17.

sentences.zh: 《大衍曆》推之，得己未冬至，後《授時》八十一刻；

translations.literal: Dayan Calendar gives jiwei winter solstice, eighty-one ke after Shoushi;
translations.idiomatic: Dayan gives jiwei, 81 ke after Shoushi;

sentences.zh: 《授時曆》上考開元丁卯歲，得己亥冬至，與《大衍曆》合，先四刻。

translations.literal: Shoushi back-calculated to Kaiyuan dingmao gives jihai winter solstice, matching Dayan, four ke earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Shoushi back-calculation matches Dayan, four ke earlier.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年辛丑歲十一月壬子日七十六刻冬至，距至元十七年庚辰歲，計四百五十九年。

translations.literal: Changqing 1 (xinchou), eleventh month, renzi day, seventy-six ke winter solstice—459 years from Zhiyuan 17.

sentences.zh: 《宣明曆》推之，得庚申冬至，後《授時》一日；

translations.literal: Xuanming Calendar gives gengshen winter solstice, one day after Shoushi;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanming gives gengshen, one day after Shoushi;

sentences.zh: 《授時曆》上考長慶辛丑歲，得壬子冬至，與《宣明曆》合。

translations.literal: Shoushi back-calculated to Changqing xinchou gives renzi winter solstice, matching Xuanming.

sentences.zh: 宋太平興國五年庚辰歲十一月丙午日六十三刻冬至，距至元十七年庚辰歲，計三百年。

translations.literal: Song Taiping Xingguo 5 (gengchen), eleventh month, bingwu day, sixty-three ke winter solstice—300 years from Zhiyuan 17.

sentences.zh: 《乾元曆》推之，得庚申冬至，後《授時》一日；

translations.literal: Qianyuan Calendar gives gengshen winter solstice, one day after Shoushi;
translations.idiomatic: Qianyuan gives gengshen, one day after Shoushi;

sentences.zh: 《授時曆》上考太平興國庚辰歲，得丙午冬至，與《乾元》合。

translations.literal: Shoushi back-calculated to Taiping Xingguo gengchen gives bingwu winter solstice, matching Qianyuan.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年庚子歲十一月辛卯日五十三刻冬至，距至元十七年庚辰歲，計二百八十年。

translations.literal: Xianping 3 (gengzi), eleventh month, xinmao day, fifty-three ke winter solstice—280 years from Zhiyuan 17.

sentences.zh: 《儀天曆》推之，得庚申冬至，後《授時》一日；

translations.literal: Yitian Calendar gives gengshen winter solstice, one day after Shoushi;
translations.idiomatic: Yitian gives gengshen, one day after Shoushi;

sentences.zh: 《授時》上考咸平庚子歲，得辛卯冬至，與《儀天》合。

translations.literal: Shoushi back-calculated to Xianping gengzi gives xinmao winter solstice, matching Yitian.

sentences.zh: 崇寧四年乙酉歲十一月辛丑日六十二刻冬至，距至元十七年庚辰歲，計一百七十五年。

translations.literal: Chongning 4 (yiyou), eleventh month, xinchou day, sixty-two ke winter solstice—175 years from Zhiyuan 17.

sentences.zh: 《紀元曆》推之，得己未日冬至，後《授時》十九刻；

translations.literal: Jiyuan Calendar gives jiwei day winter solstice, nineteen ke after Shoushi;
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan gives jiwei, 19 ke after Shoushi;

sentences.zh: 《授時曆》上考崇寧乙酉歲，得辛丑日冬至，與《紀元曆》合，先二刻。

translations.literal: Shoushi back-calculated to Chongning yiyou gives xinchou day winter solstice, matching Jiyuan, two ke earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Shoushi back-calculation matches Jiyuan, two ke earlier.

sentences.zh: 金大定十九年己亥歲十一月己巳日六十四刻冬至，距至元十七年庚辰歲，計一百一年。

translations.literal: Jin Dading 19 (jihai), eleventh month, jisi day, sixty-four ke winter solstice—101 years from Zhiyuan 17.

sentences.zh: 《大明曆》推之，得己未冬至，後《授時》一十九刻；

translations.literal: Daming Calendar gives jiwei winter solstice, nineteen ke after Shoushi;
translations.idiomatic: Daming gives jiwei, 19 ke after Shoushi;

sentences.zh: 《授時曆》上考大定己亥歲，己巳冬至，與《大明曆》合，先九刻。

translations.literal: Shoushi back-calculated to Dading jihai gives jisi winter solstice, matching Daming, nine ke earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Shoushi back-calculation matches Daming, nine ke earlier.

sentences.zh: （《大明》冬至蓋測驗未密故也。）〉

translations.literal: (Daming winter solstice likely because observation was insufficiently precise.)

sentences.zh: 慶元四年戊午歲十一月己酉日一十七刻冬至，距至元十七年庚辰歲，計八十二年。

translations.literal: Qingyuan 4 (wuwu), eleventh month, jiyou day, seventeen ke winter solstice—82 years from Zhiyuan 17.

sentences.zh: 《統天曆》推之，得己未冬至，先《授時》一刻；

translations.literal: Tongtian Calendar gives jiwei winter solstice, one ke before Shoushi;
translations.idiomatic: Tongtian gives jiwei, one ke before Shoushi;

sentences.zh: 《授時曆》上考慶元戊午歲，得己酉日冬至，與《統天曆》合。

translations.literal: Shoushi back-calculated to Qingyuan wuwu gives jiyou day winter solstice, matching Tongtian.

sentences.zh: 周天列宿度

translations.literal: Degrees of the Circuit of Heaven and the Lodges
translations.idiomatic: Circuit of Heaven and Lodge Degrees

sentences.zh: 列宿著於天，為舍二十有八，為度三百六十五有奇。

translations.literal: The lodges fixed in Heaven number twenty-eight mansions and 365-odd degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-eight lodges span 365-odd degrees across the sky.

sentences.zh: 非日躔無以校其度，非列舍無以紀其度，周天之度，因二者以得之。

translations.literal: Without the sun's lodge position one cannot verify the degrees; without the lodges one cannot record them—the circuit of Heaven is obtained through both.
translations.idiomatic: Solar motion and lodge positions together define the celestial circuit.

sentences.zh: 天體渾圓，當二極南北之中，絡以赤道，日月五星之行，常出入於比。

translations.literal: The celestial body is perfectly round; at the midpoint between the two poles the equator girdles it—the sun, moon, and five planets constantly enter and exit near it.
translations.idiomatic: The heavens are spherical, girdled by the equator; sun, moon, and planets cross it regularly.

sentences.zh: 天左旋，日月五星溯而右轉，昔人曆象日月星辰，謂此也。

translations.literal: Heaven rotates leftward; sun, moon, and planets move retrograde rightward—this is what the ancients meant by observing the calendar and the luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven spins westward; the luminaries creep eastward against it.

sentences.zh: 然列舍相距度數，歷代所測不同，非微有動移，則前人所測或有未密。

translations.literal: Yet inter-lodge distances measured by successive dynasties differ—either the lodges shift slightly, or earlier measurements were imprecise.
translations.idiomatic: Lodge intervals differ across dynasties—either precession or measurement error.

sentences.zh: 古用窺管，今新制渾儀，測用二線，所測度數分秒與前代不同者，今列於左。

translations.literal: Antiquity used sighting tubes; now a new armillary sphere uses paired threads—the measured degrees, fen, and miao differing from earlier ages are listed at left.
translations.idiomatic: New armillary measurements differ from earlier tube observations; results are tabulated below.

sentences.zh: （表略）〉

translations.literal: (table abbreviated)

sentences.zh: 日躔

translations.literal: Solar Lodge Motion

sentences.zh: 日之麗天，縣象最著，大明一生，列宿俱熄。

translations.literal: The sun adorning Heaven is the most visible suspended sign; when the Great Brightness is born, all lodges are extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Sunrise outshines every star—the brightest sign in the sky.

sentences.zh: 古人欲測躔度所在，必以昏旦夜半中星衡考其所距，從考其所當；

translations.literal: Ancients seeking the sun's lodge position had to use culminating stars at dusk, dawn, and midnight to gauge its distance and determine its place;
translations.idiomatic: Ancient method: use culminating stars at dusk, dawn, and midnight to locate solar lodge position;

sentences.zh: 然昏旦夜半時刻未易得真，時刻一差，則所距、所當，不容無舛。

translations.literal: yet true moments of dusk, dawn, and midnight were hard to obtain; one moment's error corrupts both distance and placement.
translations.idiomatic: A single timing error corrupts the whole calculation.

sentences.zh: 晉姜岌首以月食沖檢，知日度所在；

translations.literal: Jin's Jiang Ji first used lunar eclipse opposition to verify solar longitude;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji first used lunar eclipse opposition to fix solar position;

sentences.zh: 《紀元曆》復以太白誌其相距遠近，於昏後明前驗定星度，因得日躔。

translations.literal: Era Origin Calendar again used Venus to record relative distances, verifying star positions after dusk and before dawn, thereby obtaining solar lodge motion.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan Calendar used Venus distances at twilight to determine solar lodge.

sentences.zh: 今用至元丁丑四月癸酉望月食既，推求得冬至日躔赤道箕宿十度，黃道九度有奇。

translations.literal: Using the total lunar eclipse at full moon on guiyou day, fourth month of Zhiyuan dingchou, winter solstice solar lodge is calculated at ten degrees of Ji on the equator, nine-odd degrees on the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhiyuan dingchou eclipse: winter solstice at Ji 10° equatorial, 9°+ ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 仍自其年正月至己卯歲終，三年之間，日測太陰所離宿次及歲星、太白相距度，定驗參考，共得一百三十四事，皆躔箕宿，適與月食所沖允合。

translations.literal: From that year's first month through jimao year's end, over three years daily observation of the moon's lodge, and Jupiter and Venus distances, yielded 134 verification cases—all at lodge Ji, matching eclipse opposition exactly.
translations.idiomatic: Three years of observations—134 cases—all confirm Ji, matching the eclipse.

sentences.zh: 以金趙知微所修《大明曆法》推之，冬至猶躔鬥初度三十六分六十四秒，比新測實差七十六分六十四秒。

translations.literal: Projected by Jin Zhao Zhiwei's Daming Calendar method, winter solstice still falls at Dipper initial degree 36 fen 64 miao—seventy-six fen 64 miao behind new measurement.
translations.idiomatic: Daming Calendar misses by 76 fen 64 miao versus new observation.

sentences.zh: 日行盈縮

translations.literal: Solar Motion: Surplus and Deficit

sentences.zh: 日月之行，有冬有夏，言日月行度，冬夏各不同也。

translations.literal: Sun and moon travel differently in winter and summer—their daily motion differs by season.
translations.idiomatic: Solar and lunar daily motion varies between winter and summer.

sentences.zh: 人徒知日行一度，一歲一周天，曾不知盈縮損益，四序有不同者。

translations.literal: People merely know the sun moves one degree daily and circles Heaven in a year, unaware that surplus and deficit vary through the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Most know one degree per day—but not seasonal speed variation.

sentences.zh: 北齊張子信積候合蝕加時，覺日行有入氣差，然損益未得其正。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's Zhang Zixin, accumulating eclipse timings, noticed solar motion differed at qi entry—but surplus and deficit were not correctly determined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zixin noticed seasonal solar variation but could not quantify it.

sentences.zh: 趙道嚴復準晷景長短，定日行進退，更造盈縮以求虧食。

translations.literal: Zhao Daoyan again calibrated gnomon shadow length to fix solar advance and retreat, remaking surplus-deficit tables for eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Daoyan used shadow lengths to model solar speed for eclipses.

sentences.zh: 至劉焯立躔度，與四序升降，雖損益不同，後代祖述用之。

translations.literal: Liu Chuo established lodge motion with seasonal rise and fall; though surplus and deficit differ, later ages followed his method.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chuo's seasonal model became the standard for later calendars.

sentences.zh: 夫陰陽往來，馴積而變，冬至日行一度強，出赤道二十四度弱，自此日軌漸北，積八十八日九十一分，當春分前三日，交在赤道，實行九十一度三十一分而適平。

translations.literal: Yin and yang alternate, change through gradual accumulation; at winter solstice the sun moves one-odd degrees daily, twenty-four-odd degrees north of the equator; from there its path turns north; after eighty-eight days ninety-one parts, three days before equinox it crosses the equator, actually traveling ninety-one degrees thirty-one parts to reach uniform speed.
translations.idiomatic: From winter solstice the sun accelerates northward, reaching uniform speed three days before equinox.

sentences.zh: 自後其盈日損，復行九十三日七十一分，當夏至之日，入赤道內二十四度弱，實行九十一度三十一分，日行一度弱，向之盈分盡損而無余。

translations.literal: Then daily surplus diminishes; after ninety-three days seventy-one parts, at summer solstice entering twenty-four-odd degrees inside the equator, actually traveling ninety-one degrees thirty-one parts at one-odd degrees daily—the prior surplus fully exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus fades until summer solstice, when the sun slows to one-odd degrees daily.

sentences.zh: 自此日軌漸南，積九十三日七十一分，當秋分後三日，交在赤道，實行九十一度三十一分而復平。

translations.literal: From there the path turns south; after ninety-three days seventy-one parts, three days after equinox crossing the equator, actually traveling ninety-one degrees thirty-one parts back to uniform speed.
translations.idiomatic: The sun decelerates southward, regaining uniform speed three days after equinox.

sentences.zh: 自後其縮日損，行八十八日九十一分，出赤道外二十四度弱，實行九十一度三十一分，復當冬至，向之縮分盡損而無余。

translations.literal: Then daily deficit diminishes; traveling eighty-eight days ninety-one parts, twenty-four-odd degrees outside the equator, actually ninety-one degrees thirty-one parts, returning to winter solstice—the prior deficit fully exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Deficit fades until winter solstice completes the cycle.

sentences.zh: 盈縮均有損益，初為益，末為損。

translations.literal: Both surplus and deficit have increase and decrease; initially increasing, finally decreasing.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus and deficit each rise then fall.

sentences.zh: 自冬至以及春分，春分以及夏至，日躔自北陸轉而西，西而南，於盈為益，益極而損，損至於無余而縮。

translations.literal: From winter solstice through equinox to summer solstice, solar lodge turns from northern quarter westward then southward; surplus increases to its limit then decreases to zero and becomes deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Winter to summer: surplus peaks at solstice then yields to deficit.

sentences.zh: 自夏至以及秋分，秋分以及冬至，日躔自南陸轉而東，東而北，於縮為益，益極而損，損至於無余而復盈。

translations.literal: From summer solstice through equinox to winter solstice, solar lodge turns from southern quarter eastward then northward; deficit increases to its limit then decreases to zero and becomes surplus again.
translations.idiomatic: Summer to winter: deficit peaks at solstice then yields to surplus.

sentences.zh: 盈初縮末，俱八十八日九十一分而行一象；

translations.literal: Surplus beginning and deficit ending: each eighty-eight days ninety-one parts for one quadrant;
translations.idiomatic: Surplus start and deficit end: 88 days 91 parts per quadrant;

sentences.zh: 縮初盈末，俱九十三日七十一分而行一象；

translations.literal: Deficit beginning and surplus ending: each ninety-three days seventy-one parts for one quadrant;
translations.idiomatic: Deficit start and surplus end: 93 days 71 parts per quadrant;

sentences.zh: 盈縮極差，皆二度四十分。

translations.literal: Maximum surplus-deficit difference: two degrees forty fen each.

sentences.zh: 由實測晷景而得，仍以算術推考，與所測允合。

translations.literal: Obtained from measured gnomon shadows, then verified by calculation—matching observation.
translations.idiomatic: Derived from gnomon observation and confirmed by calculation.

sentences.zh: 月行遲疾

translations.literal: Lunar Motion: Slow and Fast

sentences.zh: 古曆謂月平行十三度十九分度之七。

translations.literal: Ancient calendars held the moon moves uniformly at thirteen and seven-nineteenths degrees daily.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient mean lunar motion: 13° 7/19 per day.

sentences.zh: 漢耿壽昌以為日月行至牽牛、東井，日過度，月行十五度，至婁、角，始平行，赤道使然。

translations.literal: Han's Geng Shouchang held that at Ox and Well lodges the sun overshoots and the moon moves fifteen degrees; reaching Harvester and Horn, motion becomes uniform—the equator causes this.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Shouchang attributed speed variation to equatorial latitude effects.

sentences.zh: 賈逵以為今合朔、弦、望、月食加時，所以不中者，蓋不知月行遲疾意。

translations.literal: Jia Kui held that new moon, quarter, full moon, and eclipse timings miss because the slow-fast variation of lunar motion was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui blamed timing errors on ignoring lunar anomalistic motion.

sentences.zh: 李梵、蘇統皆以月行當有遲疾，不必在牽牛、東井、婁、角之間，乃由行道有遠近出入所生。

translations.literal: Li Fan and Su Tong both held lunar motion must have slow and fast phases—not confined to Ox, Well, Harvester, and Horn—but arising from the path's varying distance and declination.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan and Su Tong traced variation to orbital distance, not fixed lodges.

sentences.zh: 劉洪作《乾象曆》，精思二十餘年，始悟其理，列為差率，以囿進退損益之數。

translations.literal: Liu Hong wrote the Supernal Icon Calendar, pondering twenty-odd years before grasping the principle, tabulating difference rates for advance-retreat surplus-deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong spent twenty years deriving lunar anomaly tables.

sentences.zh: 後之作曆者，咸因之。

translations.literal: Later calendar-makers all followed him.
translations.idiomatic: All later calendars followed his method.

sentences.zh: 至唐一行，考九道委蛇曲折之數，得月行疾徐之理。

translations.literal: Tang's Yixing, examining the winding numbers of the nine paths, grasped the principle of lunar speed variation.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing refined the theory through the nine lunar paths.

sentences.zh: 先儒謂月與五星，皆近日而疾，遠日而遲。

translations.literal: Earlier scholars held moon and five planets move faster near the sun, slower when far.
translations.idiomatic: Classical view: faster near the sun, slower when distant.

sentences.zh: 曆家立法，以入轉一周之日，為遲疾二曆，各立初末二限，初為益，末為損。

translations.literal: Calendar-makers legislate: the day of entering one anomalistic revolution forms slow-fast dual tables, each with initial and final limits—increase at start, decrease at end.
translations.idiomatic: Anomalistic month split into slow and fast tables with initial and final limits.

sentences.zh: 在疾初遲末，其行度率過於平行；

translations.literal: In fast initial and slow final phases, daily motion exceeds mean speed;
translations.idiomatic: Fast start and slow end: motion exceeds mean speed;

sentences.zh: 遲初疾末，率不及於平行。

translations.literal: slow initial and fast final phases fall below mean speed.
translations.idiomatic: Slow start and fast end: motion falls below mean speed.

sentences.zh: 自入轉初日行十四度半強，從是漸殺，曆七日，適及平行度，謂之疾初限，其積度比平行余五度四十二分。

translations.literal: From anomalistic entry the first day moves fourteen-odd degrees; gradually diminishing over seven days to mean speed—the fast initial limit; accumulated motion exceeds mean by five degrees forty-two fen.
translations.idiomatic: Fast initial limit: 7 days from 14°+ to mean, +5°42' accumulated.

sentences.zh: 自是其疾日損，又曆七日，行十二度微強，向之益者盡損而無余，謂之疾末限。

translations.literal: Then daily speed decreases; after seven more days moving twelve-odd degrees, prior surplus fully exhausted—the fast final limit.
translations.idiomatic: Fast final limit: 7 more days to 12°+, surplus exhausted.

sentences.zh: 自是復行遲度，又曆七日，適及平行度，謂之遲初限，其積度比平行不及五度四十二分。

translations.literal: Then slow motion resumes; seven days to mean speed—the slow initial limit; accumulated motion falls five degrees forty-two fen short of mean.
translations.idiomatic: Slow initial limit: 7 days to mean, −5°42' accumulated.

sentences.zh: 自此其遲日損，行度漸增，又曆七日，復行十四度半強，向之益者亦損而無余，謂之遲末限。

translations.literal: Then daily slowness diminishes, speed increasing; seven more days back to fourteen-odd degrees—prior deficit fully exhausted, the slow final limit.
translations.idiomatic: Slow final limit: 7 more days back to 14°+, deficit exhausted.

sentences.zh: 入轉一周，實二十七日五十五刻四十六分，遲疾極差皆五度四十二分。

translations.literal: One anomalistic revolution: actually twenty-seven days fifty-five ke forty-six parts; slow-fast extreme difference five degrees forty-two fen each.

sentences.zh: 舊曆日為一限，皆用二十八限。

translations.literal: Old calendars used one day per limit, twenty-eight limits total.

sentences.zh: 今定驗得轉分進退時各不同，今分日為十二，共三百三十六限，半之為半周限，析而四之為象限。

translations.literal: New verification shows entry advance-retreat times differ; now dividing the day into twelve parts, 336 limits total; halved for half-revolution limits, quartered for quadrant limits.
translations.idiomatic: New method: 336 limits (day split into twelve parts).

sentences.zh: 白道交周

translations.literal: White Path: Nodal Cycle

sentences.zh: 當二極南北之中，橫絡天體以紀宿度者，赤道也。

translations.literal: At the midpoint between the poles, horizontally girdling the heavens to mark lodge degrees—that is the equator.
translations.idiomatic: The equator girdles the heavens at the celestial midpoint.

sentences.zh: 出入赤道，為日行之軌者，黃道也。

translations.literal: Entering and exiting the equator—the sun's path—is the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: The ecliptic is the sun's path across the equator.

sentences.zh: 所謂白道，與黃道交貫，月行之所由也。

translations.literal: The so-called white path intersects the ecliptic—it is the moon's route.
translations.idiomatic: The white path (lunar orbit) crosses the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 古人隨方立名，分為八行，與黃道而九，究而言之，其實一也。

translations.literal: Ancients named paths by direction, dividing into eight routes plus the ecliptic—nine in all; in essence they are one.
translations.idiomatic: Eight directional paths plus the ecliptic are one continuous orbit.

sentences.zh: 惟其隨交遷徙，變動不居，故強以方色名之。

translations.literal: Only because it shifts with the nodes, ever changing, was it forcibly named by direction and color.
translations.idiomatic: Nodal drift forced directional color-naming on a single path.

sentences.zh: 月道出入日道，兩相交值，當朔則日為月所掩，當望則月為日所沖，故皆有食。

translations.literal: The moon's path crosses the sun's; at new moon the sun is covered, at full moon the moon is eclipsed—hence both yield eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing paths cause solar eclipses at new moon and lunar at full.

sentences.zh: 然涉交有遠近，食分有深淺，皆可以數推之。

translations.literal: Yet nodal distance varies, eclipse magnitude differs—all computable by number.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipse depth depends on nodal distance—all calculable.

sentences.zh: 所謂交周者，月道出入日道一周之日也。

translations.literal: The nodal cycle is the days for the moon's path to complete one crossing of the sun's path.
translations.idiomatic: Nodal cycle: days for the moon to recross the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 日道距赤道之遠，為度二十有四。

translations.literal: The sun's path reaches twenty-four degrees from the equator.

sentences.zh: 月道出入日道，不逾六度；

translations.literal: The moon's path crosses the sun's by no more than six degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Lunar inclination: no more than 6° from the ecliptic;

sentences.zh: 其距赤道也，遠不過三十度，近不下十八度。

translations.literal: from the equator at most thirty degrees, at least eighteen.

sentences.zh: 出黃道外為陽，入黃道內為陰，陰陽一周，分為四象。

translations.literal: Outside the ecliptic is yang, inside is yin; one yin-yang cycle divides into four quadrants.
translations.idiomatic: Outside ecliptic = yang, inside = yin; one cycle = four quadrants.

sentences.zh: 月當黃道為正交，出黃道外六度為半交，復當黃道為中交，入黃道內六度為半交，是為四象。

translations.literal: Moon on the ecliptic is major crossing; six degrees outside is half-crossing; back on ecliptic is mid-crossing; six degrees inside is half-crossing—the four quadrants.
translations.idiomatic: Major, half, mid, and half crossings define four nodal quadrants.

sentences.zh: 象別七日，各行九十一度，四象周曆，是謂一交之終，以日計之，得二十七日二十一刻二十二分二十四秒。

translations.literal: Each quadrant seven days, each moving ninety-one degrees; four quadrants complete one nodal cycle—twenty-seven days twenty-one ke twenty-two fen twenty-four miao by day count.

sentences.zh: 每一交，退天一度二百分度之九十三，凡二百四十九交，退天一周有奇，終而復始。

translations.literal: Each cycle retreats one and 93/200 degrees against the stars; 249 cycles retreat one circuit plus—then repeat.
translations.idiomatic: 249 nodal cycles = one sidereal regression of the nodes.

sentences.zh: 正交在春正，半交出黃道外六度，在赤道內十八度。

translations.literal: Major crossing at spring first month: half-crossing six degrees outside ecliptic, eighteen inside equator.
translations.idiomatic: Spring major crossing: half-point at ecliptic +6°, equator −18°.

sentences.zh: 正交在秋正，半交出黃道外六度，在赤道外三十度。

translations.literal: Major crossing at autumn first month: half-crossing six degrees outside ecliptic, thirty outside equator.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn major crossing: half-point at ecliptic +6°, equator +30°.

sentences.zh: 中交在春正，半交入黃道內六度，在赤道內三十度。

translations.literal: Mid-crossing at spring first month: half-crossing six degrees inside ecliptic, thirty inside equator.
translations.idiomatic: Spring mid-crossing: half-point at ecliptic −6°, equator −30°.

sentences.zh: 中交在秋正，半交入黃道內六度，在赤道外十八度。

translations.literal: Mid-crossing at autumn first month: half-crossing six degrees inside ecliptic, eighteen outside equator.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn mid-crossing: half-point at ecliptic −6°, equator +18°.

sentences.zh: 月道與赤道正交，距春秋二正黃赤道正交宿度，東西不及十四度三分度之二。

translations.literal: Moon path major crossing with equator falls east-west within fourteen and two-thirds degrees of the spring and autumn equinoctial colures.
translations.idiomatic: Nodal colure within 14⅔° of equinox lodges.

sentences.zh: 夏至在陰曆內，冬至在陽曆外，月道與赤道所差者多；

translations.literal: When summer solstice falls in the yin half and winter solstice in the yang half, lunar-equatorial difference is greater;
translations.idiomatic: Yin-year solstice placement increases lunar-equatorial spread;

sentences.zh: 夏至在陽曆外，冬至在陰曆內，月道與赤道所差者少。

translations.literal: when summer solstice is in the yang half and winter in the yin half, the difference is smaller.

sentences.zh: 蓋白道二交，有斜有直，陰陽二曆，有內有外，直者密而狹，斜者疏而闊，其差亦從而異。

translations.literal: The white path's two crossings may be oblique or direct; yin-yang halves may be inner or outer—direct crossings are tight and narrow, oblique ones loose and wide; differences follow accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Oblique nodes yield wider latitude variation than direct ones.

sentences.zh: 今立象置法求之，差數多者不過三度五十分，少者不下一度三十分，是為月道與赤道多少之差。

translations.literal: Setting up quadrant methods to solve: maximum difference three degrees fifty fen, minimum one degree thirty fen—the moon path's equatorial latitude range.

sentences.zh: 晝夜刻

translations.literal: Day and Night: Ke Divisions

sentences.zh: 日出為晝，日入為夜，晝夜一周，共為百刻。

translations.literal: Sunrise is day, sunset is night; one day-night cycle totals one hundred ke.

sentences.zh: 以十二辰分之，每辰得八刻三分刻之一。

translations.literal: Divided among twelve double-hours, each receives eight and one-third ke.

sentences.zh: 無間南北，所在皆同。

translations.literal: Regardless of north or south, everywhere the same.
translations.idiomatic: Uniform everywhere—or so the old view held.

sentences.zh: 晝短則夜長，夜短則晝長，此自然之理也。

translations.literal: Short day means long night, short night means long day—nature's principle.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night lengths are inversely related.

sentences.zh: 春秋二分，日當赤道出入，晝夜正等，各五十刻。

translations.literal: At spring and autumn equinoxes the sun crosses the equator; day and night equal, fifty ke each.

sentences.zh: 自春分以及夏至，日入赤道內，去極浸近，夜短而晝長。

translations.literal: From equinox to summer solstice the sun enters inside the equator, approaching the pole; nights shorten, days lengthen.
translations.idiomatic: Spring to summer: days lengthen as the sun moves north.

sentences.zh: 自秋分以及冬至，日出赤道外，去極浸遠，晝短而夜長。

translations.literal: From equinox to winter solstice the sun rises outside the equator, receding from the pole; days shorten, nights lengthen.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn to winter: nights lengthen as the sun moves south.

sentences.zh: 以地中揆之，長不過六十刻，短不過四十刻。

translations.literal: Measured from the earth's midpoint, maximum length sixty ke, minimum forty.
translations.idiomatic: At the terrestrial midpoint: 40–60 ke daylight.

sentences.zh: 地中以南，夏至去日出入之所為遠，其長有不及六十刻者；

translations.literal: South of the midpoint, summer solstice is far from sunrise and sunset points; day length may fall short of sixty ke;
translations.idiomatic: South of center: summer days may not reach 60 ke;

sentences.zh: 冬至去日出入之所為近，其短有不止四十刻者。

translations.literal: winter solstice near those points; night may exceed forty ke.

sentences.zh: 地中以北，夏至去日出入之所為近，其長有不止六十刻者；

translations.literal: North of the midpoint, summer solstice is near sunrise and sunset; day may exceed sixty ke;
translations.idiomatic: North of center: summer days may exceed 60 ke;

sentences.zh: 冬至去日出入之所為遠，其短有不及四十刻者。

translations.literal: winter solstice far from those points; night may fall short of forty ke.
translations.idiomatic: winter nights may fall short of 40 ke.

sentences.zh: 今京師冬至日出辰初二刻，日入申正二刻，故晝刻三十八，夜刻六十二；

translations.literal: At the capital, winter solstice sunrise at chen initial second ke, sunset at shen upright second ke—day thirty-eight ke, night sixty-two;
translations.idiomatic: Capital winter solstice: 38 ke day, 62 ke night;

sentences.zh: 夏至日出寅正二刻，日入戌初二刻，故晝刻六十二，夜刻三十八。

translations.literal: summer solstice sunrise at yin upright second ke, sunset at xu initial second ke—day sixty-two ke, night thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Capital summer solstice: 62 ke day, 38 ke night.

sentences.zh: 蓋地有南北，極有高下，日出入有早晏，所以不同耳。

translations.literal: Earth has north and south, the pole has height, sunrise and sunset have early and late—hence the difference.
translations.idiomatic: Latitude and polar height account for the variation.

sentences.zh: 今《授時曆》晝夜刻，一以京師為正，其各所實測北極高下，具見《天文志》。

translations.literal: Shoushi Calendar day-night ke divisions take the capital as standard; measured polar heights for each location appear in the Treatise on Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Shoushi uses the capital standard; local polar heights are in the Astronomy Treatise.
